summary: Introduces LatentGUIWorld to test learning interface semantics and dynamics through interaction, and studies finer movement actions with intermediate visual feedback and exploration demonstrations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: PrivacyGuard: Source-Linked Sanitization and Locally Resolvable PII References for Cloud GUI Agents
summary: Introduces PrivacyGuard, which sanitizes source-linked personal information and maintains locally resolvable references across mobile-agent turns to reduce exposure to remote planners.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: BrowseSafe++: Benchmarking Prompt Injection Detection Across Web Contexts, Languages, and Browser Views
summary: Extends BrowseSafe with paired attacked and clean webpages in several representations, and studies text and screenshot detectors plus feedback-adapted prompt injections.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: OpenMobile-2: Building Versatile Mobile Agents with Scalable Environments and App-Native Tools
summary: Introduces OpenMobile-2, combining simulated mobile apps, emulator tasks, released training data, and policies that can alternate GUI interaction with app-native tools.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GroundGUI training and evaluation code
summary: Code for screenshot grounding through supervised training, teacher-guided distillation, reinforcement learning, and benchmark evaluation.
notes: The repository documents separate training-stage environments. Code, model weights, and ScreenRef data have distinct license declarations.

name: ScreenRef
summary: GUI screenshots paired with localization instructions and targets, including absent-target examples; image access is gated under publisher terms.

dataset_profile.notes: The publisher reports these inventories in the companion annotation card. The refusal subset is included in the full recipe. Screenshot access is gated; no image download or independent corpus recount was performed.

notes: The public Hub API reports gated=auto and a Restricted Research-Only declaration. The companion card distinguishes annotations from screenshots and limits reuse. Access terms were inspected as public metadata; no access agreement was accepted or gated files downloaded.

name: ScreenRef Annotations
summary: Annotation files, task recipes, and image manifests for ScreenRef; screenshots reside in the separately gated image repository.

dataset_profile.notes: The recipes reuse source images and are not additive datasets. This download contains no screenshots. Counts are publisher-reported; rows named for trajectories are independent decision examples, not full trajectories.

notes: The card declares restricted academic research use and no redistribution. Annotation coordinates use a normalized 1000 by 1000 space. Some source instructions name gestures other than the single-click target; the publisher recommends treating those as location supervision.

name: GroundGUI RL Dataset
summary: Desktop grounding prompts selected from GroundCUA and formatted for click-based reinforcement learning with target-box rewards.

dataset_profile.notes: Publisher-reported counts cover a selection and reformatting of GroundCUA, not a new disjoint image collection. No independent image-overlap audit was performed.

notes: The card declares MIT and attributes the source examples to GroundCUA. Its separate claim about UI-Vision overlap is not independently validated by this catalog.

name: Seg2Click
summary: Training and inference implementation that predicts an executable-region mask and derives a GUI click from that mask.
notes: The repository provides training, evaluation, and a custom mask decoder. Its code license does not determine the licenses of the five model checkpoints. No model execution was performed.

name: GroundGUI-8B
summary: Screenshot grounding checkpoint that emits a single click in a normalized coordinate space.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data.

name: Seg2Click Qwen3.5 0.8B
summary: Compact Seg2Click checkpoint with a merged Qwen3.5 backbone and an action-mask decoder.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data. The checkpoint includes a merged backbone and mask decoder; a generic text-generation pipeline alone does not implement mask-to-click inference.

name: Seg2Click Qwen3.5 2B
summary: Seg2Click checkpoint using a 2B Qwen3.5 backbone to predict a mask and select an interface click.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data. The checkpoint includes a merged backbone and mask decoder; a generic text-generation pipeline alone does not implement mask-to-click inference.

name: Seg2Click Qwen2.5-VL 3B
summary: Seg2Click checkpoint based on Qwen2.5-VL-3B with a custom action-mask decoder.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data. The checkpoint includes a merged backbone and mask decoder; a generic text-generation pipeline alone does not implement mask-to-click inference. The card names the Qwen Research license, unlike the Apache-2.0 declarations on the Qwen3.5 variants.

name: Seg2Click Qwen3.5 4B
summary: Seg2Click checkpoint pairing a 4B Qwen3.5 backbone with pixel-level action-mask prediction.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data. The checkpoint includes a merged backbone and mask decoder; a generic text-generation pipeline alone does not implement mask-to-click inference.

name: Seg2Click Qwen3.5 9B
summary: Seg2Click checkpoint pairing a 9B Qwen3.5 backbone with a decoder for valid GUI click regions.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data. The checkpoint includes a merged backbone and mask decoder; a generic text-generation pipeline alone does not implement mask-to-click inference.

name: OpenMobile-2 9B
summary: Mobile-agent checkpoint trained on OpenMobile-Data-v2 for screenshot actions and app-native tool calls.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data.

name: OpenMobile-2 27B
summary: Mobile-agent checkpoint based on Qwen3.6-27B for GUI and app-native tool interaction.

details.artifact_inspection: Public file-manifest inspection only; weights were not downloaded.

notes: License declarations apply to this checkpoint separately from code and training data.

name: SwitchMem
summary: Memory-routing implementation that chooses text or image demonstrations for a frozen GUI actor, with offline evaluation and Android transfer experiments.
notes: The implementation distinguishes step-level AITW/LearnGUI scores from terminal task success on MobileMiniWoB++. Benchmark outcomes and local smoke-test outputs are different claims.

name: OpenMobile-2 code
summary: Evaluation adapters and training guidance for OpenMobile-2 across Android emulators and browser-rendered mobile simulation.
notes: The README marks evaluation code, checkpoints, environments, and data as released; data-construction scripts and other resources remain pending. Each benchmark runtime is started separately. Code terms do not establish dataset permissions.

name: MobileGym++ / MobileGym++ Bench
summary: Browser-rendered mobile simulation with resettable app state and a shared task suite for GUI-only and GUI-plus-tool agents.

actions: foreground-app tool calls in hybrid mode
benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Programmatic checkers inspect changes in application state; both modes share task definitions and initial states.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The task count was checked against unique task_id values in the published manifest. The 35 new clients are a subset of 63 total clients. This simulator runs in a browser; Android-emulator apps are a separate part of OpenMobile-2.

notes: These clients simulate named commercial applications and are not those commercial products. The code and simulator data have distinct license files. No benchmark run was performed. The README describes a phone that runs in the browser, and the Android-emulator playground is a separate OpenMobile2 release, so the platform facet is web rather than a mobile operating system.

name: OpenMobile-Data-v2
summary: Mobile-agent supervision from emulator and simulator trajectories, plus executable tasks with starting states and success checks for reinforcement learning.

dataset_profile.notes: These are publisher-reported totals at three distinct grains, not values to sum. Earlier screenshots may be collapsed; each SFT example keeps at most three images. The card and repository disagree on the singular/plural RL filename, so consumers should inspect the actual file manifest.

notes: The reviewed card contains no explicit license declaration, so data-license status remains unknown. The repository code license is not inherited. The current code README points to the v2 dataset; an older project-page URL was not counted as a separate asset.

name: CarryOn implementation release
summary: Announced context runtime for maintaining reusable task objects across long agent sessions.
notes: The project README states that code will be released after review.
review_note: Primary README reviewed; implementation release is still pending. The paper is cataloged separately.

name: GraceBench task and evaluation release
summary: Announced Android execution-stability benchmark with graph-aligned trajectory diagnosis.
notes: The primary page reports 169 tasks but says code and data are coming soon.
review_note: Primary project page reviewed; task definitions, data, and evaluation-code release remain pending. The paper is cataloged separately.

name: An Illusion of Progress? Assessing the Current State of Web Agents
summary: Introduces Online-Mind2Web, with 300 tasks across 136 live websites, and examines how benchmark design affects assessments of web agents. It also develops an LLM judge for task completion and compares its judgments with human evaluation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Are Autonomous Web Agents Good Testers?
summary: Adapts web agents to execute natural-language test steps, verify assertions, and issue test verdicts. The study introduces 113 passing and failing test cases across three offline web applications and compares two agent implementations with qualitative failure analysis.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ReuseDroid: A VLM-empowered Android UI Test Migrator Boosted by Active Feedback
summary: ReuseDroid migrates Android GUI tests between functionally similar apps using VLM agents that separate shared test intent from app-specific interaction flows. It introduces LinPro, a dataset of 578 migration tasks across 39 apps, to evaluate test transfer.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. The platform or GUI evaluation setting was additionally checked in the primary full text.

name: On the Robustness of GUI Grounding Models Against Image Attacks
summary: Evaluates GUI grounding models under natural image noise, untargeted adversarial perturbations, and targeted image attacks. Experiments cover mobile, desktop, and web interfaces and analyze sensitivity to image resolution and adversarial changes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SkillWeaver: Web Agents can Self-Improve by Discovering and Honing Skills
summary: SkillWeaver explores websites, practices interactions, and converts the resulting experience into a reusable library of callable skill APIs. Its WebArena and live-website experiments examine skill refinement, composition, and transfer from stronger agents to weaker ones.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: AgentRewardBench: Evaluating Automatic Evaluations of Web Agent Trajectories
summary: AgentRewardBench evaluates automated web-agent judges against expert reviews of 1,302 trajectories from five benchmarks. The annotations cover completion, side effects, and repetition, enabling comparison of LLM judges and rule-based task evaluators.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Explorer: Robust Collection of Interactable GUI Elements
summary: Explorer collects interactable GUI elements from a live target application and records user sessions for application-specific model training. It links repeated interface states into a navigation map that supports path planning and voice-directed interaction.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Breaking the Data Barrier -- Building GUI Agents Through Task Generalization
summary: Studies whether mid-training on GUI perception, multimodal reasoning, and text reasoning transfers to GUI-agent planning. Experiments compare 11 task sources and curated mixtures using WebArena and AndroidWorld to investigate training-data choices when GUI trajectories are scarce.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: RealWebAssist: A Benchmark for Long-Horizon Web Assistance with Real-World Users
summary: RealWebAssist evaluates web assistance through sequences of instructions collected from real users across multiple websites. It tests intent interpretation, user-specific routines, long-term context, and visual grounding when instructions are ambiguous or evolve during interaction.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UI-E2I-Synth: Advancing GUI Grounding with Large-Scale Instruction Synthesis
summary: UI-E2I-Synth uses GPT-4o to synthesize GUI grounding instructions with varied complexity, addressing small elements, imbalanced element types, and implicit requests. The accompanying UI-I2E-Bench evaluates instruction-to-element localization across these annotation challenges.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: VLM-Fuzz: Vision Language Model Assisted Recursive Depth-first Search Exploration for Effective UI Testing of Android Apps
summary: VLM-Fuzz combines depth-first UI exploration with Android manifest analysis, runtime widget hierarchies, and on-demand visual reasoning to generate app test inputs. It evaluates coverage on 59 benchmark apps and uses additional Google Play apps to study crash discovery.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: WebRollback: Enhancing Web Agents with Explicit Rollback Mechanisms
summary: WebRollback gives a web agent an explicit action for returning to an earlier state in its navigation trajectory. It studies this recovery mechanism on two live web-navigation benchmarks under both zero-shot and fine-tuned settings.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: TongUI: Internet-Scale Trajectories from Multimodal Web Tutorials for Generalized GUI Agents
summary: TongUI converts multimodal online tutorials, including videos and articles, into GUI-agent trajectories. Its GUI-Net dataset contains 143,000 trajectories spanning five operating systems and more than 200 applications, and supports fine-tuning for grounding and navigation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: LearnAct: Few-Shot Mobile GUI Agent with a Unified Demonstration Benchmark
summary: LearnAct parses human demonstrations into reusable knowledge, retrieves relevant examples, and uses them during mobile GUI task execution. The accompanying LearnGUI benchmark includes 2,252 offline tasks and 101 online tasks for studying adaptation from demonstrations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ViMo: A Generative Visual GUI World Model for App Agents
summary: ViMo predicts the next mobile-app screenshot after a candidate action by separately modeling graphics and text. A symbolic placeholder representation preserves layout while a second predictor supplies readable text, enabling visual lookahead for GUI-agent planning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ScaleTrack: Scaling and back-tracking Automated GUI Agents
summary: ScaleTrack combines a unified collection of GUI grounding samples with a planning objective that predicts the next action while reconstructing prior actions. This backward prediction links the current screenshot to interaction history during agent training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Visual Test-time Scaling for GUI Agent Grounding
summary: RegionFocus adds visual test-time scaling by zooming into selected screenshot regions and maintaining an image-based map of landmarks and actions. It evaluates this grounding procedure with UI-TARS and Qwen2.5-VL on ScreenSpot-Pro and WebVoyager.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Mobile-Bench-v2: A More Realistic and Comprehensive Benchmark for VLM-based Mobile Agents
summary: Mobile-Bench-v2 evaluates mobile GUI agents using multiple acceptable offline action paths, noisy interfaces with ads or pop-ups, and ambiguous instructions with scripted clarification exchanges. These splits separate step-level execution, robustness, and proactive interaction.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MobileIPL: Enhancing Mobile Agents Thinking Process via Iterative Preference Learning
summary: MobileIPL samples trees of action-planning thoughts, propagates rule-based leaf rewards backward, and forms preference pairs for reasoning-level optimization. It also expands screenshot-based instruction data through staged evolution before evaluation on mobile GUI-agent benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Enhancing Visual Grounding for GUI Agents via Self-Evolutionary Reinforcement Learning
summary: Proposes GUI grounding training that combines curated seed examples, continuous location-dependent policy feedback, and iterative refinement guided by attention maps. The study evaluates the resulting reinforcement-learning procedure on three grounding benchmarks, including ScreenSpot-Pro.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-Shift: Enhancing VLM-Based GUI Agents through Self-supervised Reinforcement Learning
summary: GUI-Shift trains an inverse-dynamics task that predicts the initial action connecting two GUI states, using trajectories without natural-language instructions. It combines rule-based reinforcement learning with data filtering and evaluates transfer to Android automation and screenshot grounding.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Efficient Agent Training for Computer Use
summary: PC Agent-E augments 312 human computer-use trajectories with alternative action decisions synthesized by Claude 3.7 Sonnet. It studies training with this combination and introduces WindowsAgentArena-V2 as an updated evaluation benchmark.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Building a Stable Planner: An Extended Finite State Machine Based Planning Module for Mobile GUI Agent
summary: SPlanner models mobile-app functions and configurations with extended finite-state machines, traverses them to construct execution paths, and converts those paths into natural-language plans. A VLM follows these plans to perform GUI actions, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Web-Shepherd: Advancing PRMs for Reinforcing Web Agents
summary: Web-Shepherd is a process reward model for assessing individual steps of web-navigation trajectories. It introduces a collection of 40,000 step-level preference pairs with checklists and a separate benchmark for comparing reward models, then evaluates verification during WebArena-lite navigation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ARPO:End-to-End Policy Optimization for GUI Agents with Experience Replay
summary: ARPO extends group-relative policy optimization with a replay buffer that reuses successful GUI trajectories across training iterations. It filters tasks using baseline performance and compares end-to-end reinforcement learning with offline preference optimization on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-explorer: Autonomous Exploration and Mining of Transition-aware Knowledge for GUI Agent
summary: GUI-explorer generates exploration goals from screenshots and interface structure, then mines observation-action-outcome triples for app-specific transition knowledge. The resulting training-free agent uses this knowledge during mobile task execution, evaluated on SPA-Bench and AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ProgRM: Build Better GUI Agents with Progress Rewards
summary: ProgRM predicts per-step task completion progress to provide intermediate rewards during online GUI-agent training. It derives progress labels by using longest common subsequences to identify key trajectory steps, allowing useful partial progress to contribute even when a trajectory ultimately fails.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: LiteCUA: Computer as MCP Server for Computer-Use Agent on AIOS
summary: AIOS 1.0 exposes computer states and actions through an MCP server to provide structured environmental context for agents. LiteCUA is a lightweight agent built on this interface, evaluated on OSWorld to study the effect of computer-environment contextualization.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ScienceBoard: Evaluating Multimodal Autonomous Agents in Realistic Scientific Workflows
summary: ScienceBoard combines an interactive environment with professional scientific software and 169 human-curated tasks in areas including biochemistry, astronomy, and geoinformatics. It evaluates computer-use agents on visually rich research workflows and analyzes their execution limitations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-Reflection: Empowering Multimodal GUI Models with Self-Reflection Behavior
summary: GUI-Reflection synthesizes reflection and error-correction examples from successful trajectories and adds dedicated learning stages for these behaviors. It introduces a reflection task suite, a mobile environment for online data collection, and iterative reflection tuning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: BacktrackAgent: Enhancing GUI Agent with Error Detection and Backtracking Mechanism
summary: BacktrackAgent adds verification, judgment, and reflection modules to detect erroneous GUI actions and guide recovery. It develops backtracking-oriented training data that includes post-action pages and evaluates task completion and step accuracy on Mobile3M and Auto-UI.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UI-Genie: A Self-Improving Approach for Iteratively Boosting MLLM-based Mobile GUI Agents
summary: UI-Genie jointly improves a mobile GUI agent and a reward model that processes screenshots with interaction history and supplies action- and task-level feedback. Its data pipeline uses rule-based verification, corrupted trajectories, and hard negatives to support reward-guided exploration and iterative training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: RedTeamCUA: Realistic Adversarial Testing of Computer-Use Agents in Hybrid Web-OS Environments
summary: RedTeamCUA combines a virtual-machine OS environment with containerized websites for controlled prompt-injection tests spanning both interfaces. Its RTC-Bench contains 864 examples and can initialize agents at injection points to separate attack susceptibility from navigation failures.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Surfer-H Meets Holo1: Cost-Efficient Web Agent Powered by Open Weights
summary: Describes Surfer-H, a web agent paired with the Holo1 vision-language model family trained on web content, synthetic examples, and agent-generated data. The work introduces WebClick for web-interface localization and evaluates browser task execution on WebVoyager.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Go-Browse: Training Web Agents with Structured Exploration
summary: Go-Browse frames web-environment exploration as graph search so that information can be reused across data-collection episodes. It collects 10,000 successful trajectories and 40,000 interaction steps on WebArena and uses them to fine-tune a web agent.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: macOSWorld: A Multilingual Interactive Benchmark for GUI Agents
summary: macOSWorld provides 202 interactive tasks across 30 applications, with instructions and operating-system interfaces in five languages. It evaluates GUI agents on macOS workflows and includes a separate subset for deception-attack testing.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MCPWorld: A Unified Benchmarking Testbed for API, GUI, and Hybrid Computer Use Agents
summary: MCPWorld evaluates API, GUI, and hybrid computer-use agents with 201 tasks in applications whose source can be instrumented and extended with MCP support. It verifies completion from application behavior and packages the testbed in containers with GPU support.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract. The platform or GUI evaluation setting was additionally checked in the primary full text.

name: Mirage-1: Augmenting and Updating GUI Agent with Hierarchical Multimodal Skills
summary: Mirage-1 organizes interaction trajectories into execution, core, and meta-skills, then uses them to guide Monte Carlo tree search during online GUI tasks. It introduces AndroidLH for long-horizon evaluation and tests the approach on Android and web-navigation benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: LPO: Towards Accurate GUI Agent Interaction via Location Preference Optimization
summary: Location Preference Optimization uses an information-entropy signal to select interaction regions and a distance-based reward to assess click locations. It trains GUI localization through preference optimization and evaluates both offline grounding and online interaction.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: OSWorld-Human: Benchmarking the Efficiency of Computer-Use Agents
summary: OSWorld-Human adds human-determined trajectories to OSWorld to evaluate the efficiency of desktop computer-use agents. The study compares 16 agents and analyzes model-call latency, changes in step duration during task execution, and excess action steps.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: The Agent Clicks Approve: Injected Page Text Makes Browser Agents Authorize Access the Task Never Named
summary: Studies prompt-injected account-access approvals in browser agents and proposes a service-side authority envelope that checks authorization requests against the user task before allowing them to complete.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: When Charts Deceive Web Agents: A Paired Benchmark for Misleading Visualization-Grounded Tasks
summary: Introduces MisVisAgentBench, a paired executable benchmark that changes chart evidence while holding web tasks fixed, to trace how misleading visualizations affect agent decisions and downstream actions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CaptchaAgent: Verifiable Visual Reasoning for CAPTCHA Solving
summary: Presents CaptchaAgent, which builds an explicit visual representation of objects and relations, refines ambiguous regions, and checks counterfactual consistency before acting on interactive CAPTCHAs.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ConClick: Element-Wise Contrastive Learning Improves GUI Grounding
summary: Analyzes recurring distractor clicks in GUI grounding and introduces ConClick, a contrastive training method built from target–distractor pairs. Its ReClick inference procedure revisits candidate regions and compares competing predictions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Web$hell: A Unified Interface for Agentic Web Access
summary: Introduces Web$hell, an interface that compiles live pages into persistent information and action objects so agents can gather evidence, navigate websites, and reuse acquired content through shared operations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: A Baseline Assessment for the Agentic Web Technology Stack
summary: Presents MASTIF, a framework for comparing combinations of agent models, protocols, and implementation frameworks on web tasks, with an initial assessment using 300 Mind2Web tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Latent World Action Model for GUI Agents
summary: Replaces future-screenshot generation with a shared latent representation for GUI action selection and action-conditioned transition prediction. An action-aware contrastive objective encourages the transition representation to retain discriminative action-induced changes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: AgentHorizon: Evaluating Agentic Judges for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Tasks
summary: Introduces AgentHorizon, a benchmark for judging long computer-use trajectories using closely related instructions paired with recorded actions and screenshots. It tests whether judges can detect constraint violations and distinguish successful tasks from similar but incompatible requests.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: DeltaReplay: Task-Relative Memory Reuse for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Introduces DeltaReplay, which stores mobile GUI trajectories as transition graphs and decides at each step whether to reuse an action, substitute task-specific parameters, or defer to the base agent. This supports reuse of partially matching experiences without rewriting stored memory.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Right Screen, Wrong Transition: World Models as Verifiers for GUI Agents
summary: Presents LGWM, a decoder-free GUI world model that predicts the next screen representation from an action and compares it with the observed state to verify transitions. Its paired diagnostic separates legitimate and hijacked transitions that lead to the same credential screen.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SoftwareGym: Scaling Computer-Use Agent Training with Diverse Synthesized Software Environments
summary: Introduces SoftwareGym, a pipeline that synthesizes runnable GUI applications and iteratively repairs them using execution checks. It also provides a task benchmark and studies whether training on synthesized application trajectories transfers to other computer-use environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Adversarial Images Hijack Web Agents from Visual Grounding to Browser Execution
summary: Introduces WebMirage, a visual red-teaming framework that models webpage element competition and action post-processing to test whether manipulated grounding decisions lead to executed browser actions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Secure-CUA: Controlling Untrusted Influence in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Proposes Secure-CUA, which commits to per-action transactions before reading untrusted page content and separates content queries from GUI target selection. The paper formalizes its protection assumptions and evaluates benign task utility on WebArena.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Can Agents Work for Everyone? Cross-User Reliability for Mobile GUI Agents in Personalized User Interfaces
summary: Introduces PAIR for controlled evaluation of mobile GUI agents across user-conditioned application states and RePAIR for training from cross-user subgoal outcomes. The study examines failures when personalized interfaces change which items an agent must identify.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: AdvSim2Real : Training Web Agents Against Adaptive Prompt Injection in a Web World Model
summary: Presents AdvSim2Real, which jointly adapts web-task curricula, prompt-injection adversaries, and agent policies inside a frozen web world model. It evaluates robustness against an unseen adversary and transfer from simulated interaction to a real browser.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Imagine to Act: High-Fidelity Data Synthesis via Image Editing World Model for Scalable GUI Agent Training
summary: Introduces Infinite-Dreamer, which learns action-conditioned screenshot editing from structured descriptions of GUI changes and uses it to synthesize robustness examples and multi-step trajectories. The synthetic data trains a mobile GUI agent evaluated on AndroidWorld, MobileWorld, and AndroidControl-Curated.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CLIFT: Conformal Self-Verification for Web Agent Training and Test-Time Scaling
summary: Introduces CLIFT, which certifies agent-generated verification signals against training-time judges and reuses them for per-step rewards and trajectory selection. At inference, a frozen question bank helps compare candidate web rollouts without querying an external judge.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: AMBER: Training Long-Horizon Web Agents through Append-Only Memory
summary: Introduces AMBER, an append-only memory framework in which a web agent learns to reason, act, and retain evidence using outcome-reward reinforcement learning. It studies whether preserving entries avoids the loss of facts and corrective feedback seen with rewritten memory.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Decoupling What from Where: How Should a Small GUI Grounding Model Receive the Action Type?
summary: Compares ways to condition a small GUI grounding model on action type under matched training conditions on Android in the Wild. The study traces apparent gains to a coordinate-serialization choice and reports limited evidence that the gains persist with predicted action types.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Recurrent Latent Visual Search for GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces ReLaViS, which performs recurrent visual search inside a grounding model by repeatedly querying screenshot tokens and feeding the resulting spatial evidence back into the model. Coarse-to-fine supervision is constructed from existing interface-element annotations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: TeleTune: Evolving Agent Skills From Offline Telemetry
summary: Introduces TeleTune, which edits a textual skill library using held-out action prediction on offline software-use logs with missing goals or interleaved tasks. The learned workflows also guide retrieval of demonstrations for subsequent web-agent execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: When to Compile a Computer-Use Agent? Measuring Payback and Making Compilation Decisions for Token Efficiency
summary: Introduces PACE, a protocol and online decision rule for deciding when repeated GUI procedures are worth compiling into programs. It accounts for failed compilation attempts, measured per-use savings, uncertain reuse, and execution costs under an explicit cumulative budget.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: WebFovea: When the Model Is Right but the Click Is Wrong -- Reliable Round Trips for Vision-Based Web Agents on Live Websites
summary: Describes WebFovea, a vision-based live-web agent whose execution loop checks action parsing, browser effects, feedback accuracy, and observation delivery. The report analyzes failures such as coordinate mismatches and silent control interactions and documents corresponding harness changes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Securing Computer-Use Agents Against Branch Steering Attacks
summary: Introduces STEER-Bench to study branch-steering attacks that manipulate untrusted web data toward hazardous paths already permitted by an agent’s plan. Its COBRA architecture combines trusted branching plans with advance constraints on the parameters and destinations each branch can use.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: AutoGUIWorld: Image Generators as Visual World Models for GUI Agent
summary: Introduces AutoGUIWorld, which combines task planning and image editing to synthesize action-grounded GUI trajectories without running the depicted software. It filters generated transitions and tests whether training on them improves agents operating real desktop and scientific applications.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Auditing Web Agent Evaluation on WebArena-Lite: Human Review of Outcomes and Trajectories
summary: Audits WebArena-Lite outcomes and trajectories with human review to identify automatic-evaluator false negatives and the first consequential execution errors. It also studies explicit execution-state memory and procedural guidance, showing why final task scores can miss substantial differences in agent behavior.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Not All Experience Belongs in the Weights: Component Routing for Self-Improving GUI Agents
summary: Studies how to route different parts of GUI experience into model weights or runtime context rather than treating whole trajectories as a single unit. It separates locators, procedures, state facts, and lessons, then predicts their destination from recurrence and dependence on the current state.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Action Conditioned Bisimulation For GUI Agent Memory
summary: Defines a GUI-memory merge rule that treats two states as equivalent only when shared actions lead to matching outcomes and successor states. The training-free method replaces observation-similarity merging and is tested in closed-loop MiniWoB++ interaction.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Talk2Agent: Benchmarking Voice Interfaces for Text Agents
summary: Introduces Talk2Agent, a benchmark of spoken instructions for computer-use tasks that measures whether voice interfaces preserve task-critical information. It pairs human speech with an execution-free intention-based metric and checks how that metric relates to downstream task completion.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Learning Reliable GUI Agents under Imperfect Priors
summary: Combines structured GUI exploration with training designed to tolerate imperfect retrieved experience. It builds state-transition graphs and synthetic task trajectories, then injects realistic forms of interface drift so agents learn when to rely on or reject prior guidance.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ComputerSD: Online Self-Distillation from Real-Time Feedback for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces ComputerSD, which turns feedback from executed GUI transitions into online self-distillation guidance and step-level scores. A GUI analyzer supplies these signals, which are combined with trajectory-level reinforcement learning in asynchronous training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: AdaptArena: Evaluating Test-Time Personalization of Web Agents
summary: Introduces AdaptArena to test whether web agents can infer unstated user preferences from relevant past trajectories and carry those preferences into new tasks. Its AdaptiveAgent baseline separates preference-retrieval challenges from failures in downstream web execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: PrecogUI: Proactive GUI Agents via Pre-cognitive Simulation and Experience Retrieval
summary: Presents PrecogUI, which retrieves prior anomaly and success patterns and predicts symbolic UI transitions before choosing actions. It also introduces InterfereBench, generated for evaluating long GUI workflows with disruptive events and recovery requirements.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Neuro-Symbolic Computer Use: Learning Reusable Policies for Reliable and Efficient Execution
summary: Learns reusable computer-use policies that encode stable workflow logic in programs while delegating grounding and state checks to neural models. Policy iteration executes variants, diagnoses failures, revises the program, and adds verification before state-changing actions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SCA: Spatial Credit Assignment for Reinforcement Learning of GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Spatial Credit Assignment, which uses click coordinates to refine group-relative reinforcement-learning updates for GUI grounding. It distinguishes failed clicks by spatial evidence while leaving the deployed action policy unchanged.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MatToolBench: Benchmarking Multimodal Agents in Real-World Materials Science Workflows
summary: Introduces MatToolBench, a Windows-based materials-science benchmark combining GUI operation, scientific-software scripting, and database queries. Expert-defined subcriteria support partial-credit scoring, while the evaluation examines domain knowledge gaps and cross-tool handoff failures.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Absorbed in Inertia: Activation Analysis for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Studies repetitive, unproductive actions in desktop agents through their internal activation states. It proposes Reset, Reroute, Restore, a context intervention that temporarily resets an agent’s trajectory and later restores it to help escape repeated ineffective behavior.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUITAR: Structured Failure Diagnosis of GUI Agents via State Transitions
summary: Introduces GUITAR, which groups visually different screens into functional states and analyzes agent failures over a state-transition graph. It uses the resulting bottlenecks to diagnose recurring mobile and web errors and evaluate targeted guidance.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Same Tasks, Different Apps: Why Mobile GUI Agents Fail to Generalize?
summary: Introduces AnyAppBench, a live Android benchmark that holds user goals fixed while changing the application used to achieve them. It combines category-controlled task pairs with failure annotations to distinguish task understanding from application-specific execution skill.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: One Rollout Is All You Get: Fully Test-Time Adaptation for GUI Agents
summary: Defines a test-time adaptation setting with one counted attempt per arriving GUI task and no ground-truth feedback. Its SOLO method filters or relabels completed episodes, then updates a small adapter from a short window of the agent’s own experience.
verify_terms: One Rollout Is All You G
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: WebRL
summary: Training pipeline that evolves web tasks from prior attempts and uses an outcome reward model to refine browser policies.
notes: Training code and checkpoint links are released. No root code-license declaration was found in the inspected repository metadata; bundled dependency licenses do not establish a license for the whole project. Weights have separate Hub terms.

name: Proposer-Agent-Evaluator (PAE)
summary: A browser-agent training system that proposes tasks, collects visual interaction trajectories, and uses automated evaluation to drive policy improvement.
notes: Source code and browser-environment modules are present. The repository LICENSE is CC-BY-NC-4.0, while its README describes that license as applying to a dataset, leaving code scope ambiguous. The separately linked dataset is gated and was not accessed; model and dataset terms must be checked separately.

name: TAG attention-driven GUI grounding
summary: Grounding and evaluation code that aggregates a pretrained vision-language model’s attention maps to localize requested interface elements without fine-tuning.
notes: The release contains grounding and benchmark evaluation code. The inspected root repository metadata does not declare a code license. It uses external pretrained models rather than publishing a new trained checkpoint, and the README restricts redistribution of unzipped benchmark data.

name: Plan-and-Act
summary: A web-agent framework that separates high-level planning from action execution, with replanning and synthetic planner-data generation components.
notes: Runnable entry points, framework modules and synthetic-data tooling are published. The repository code declares MIT; separate model and dataset cards have their own declarations. Its setup targets WebArena-Lite and requires that external environment.

name: StateAct
summary: State-tracking prompts and experiment runners for language agents, including a WebShop implementation alongside text-based environments.
notes: The repository contains a WebShop runner as well as ALFWorld and TextCraft experiments. Inclusion concerns its web-shopping interaction component. No code license or downloadable trained checkpoint is declared in the inspected root metadata.

name: SpiritSight-Agent 8B base
summary: An InternVL2-based visual GUI checkpoint distributed for grounding and interface navigation, with the publisher recommending task-specific fine-tuning of the base release.
notes: The Hub manifest exposes four safetensors shards under SpiritSight-Agent-8B-base. The card declares Apache-2.0 and separately links InternVL terms in its model table. This is the published base checkpoint; benchmark-specific fine-tuning is discussed separately. No model code was executed.

name: GUI-Lasagne L1
summary: The published GUI-Lasagne training-data collection used for SpiritSight, distributed as dated archive shards for visual interface learning.
notes: Public archive shards are present. The dataset card declares Apache-2.0; it does not resolve rights in third-party interface content. The short card supplies no reliable sample count or explicit train/test partition, so these remain unspecified. The dataset card and archive inventory do not establish its platform distribution; the associated model's platform coverage is not inherited. An associated SpiritSight model card still describes dataset release as forthcoming; the independent dataset card and public archive manifest establish this release's availability.

name: DroidCall data
summary: Instruction-to-function-call examples for learning Android intent invocation, with training, testing and API-annotation files for mobile task execution.
notes: The release provides JSONL data and API annotations. This is Android intent-calling supervision rather than screenshot-and-click trajectories, so it is marked adjacent. The dataset card declares Apache-2.0; the companion repository’s MIT code license is a separate declaration.

name: UICrit

Its README establishes mobile interfaces without naming an operating system.

name: VideoCAD training and evaluation code

notes: Model, data-loader, preprocessing and evaluation source files are released. The reviewed root metadata has no code-license declaration. name: WebAgent-R1

notes: The implementation is inside the WebAgent-R1 subdirectory and includes training, evaluation and WebArena setup components. Root source licensing is Apache-2.0. No downloadable author checkpoint was established by the reviewed README, so this entry represents code.

name: WorkForceAgent-R1

notes: The release contains WorkArena preprocessing and training source. The inspected root has no explicit project license; dependencies retain their own terms. Although the README discusses trained 7B/14B models, it does not provide a verified checkpoint release, so this is cataloged only as a framework.

name: Agent-R
summary: Trajectory collection and revision utilities that use tree search and model-guided critique to train agents to recover from mistakes, including WebShop tasks.
notes: The canonical repository is ByteDance-Seed/Agent-R and is archived but readable. MCTS collection, revision and evaluation scripts are released under Apache-2.0. It also supports non-GUI text environments; this entry covers its WebShop interaction component. No separate weight release was verified.

name: PAE LLaVA 7B
summary: A released LLaVA checkpoint for visual browser interaction from the PAE autonomous task-proposal and policy-learning system.
notes: The model is publicly ungated and has seven safetensors shards plus tokenizer and configuration files. Its card declares CC-BY-NC-4.0 for this model. This weight declaration does not settle the separate PAE dataset or code licensing questions.

name: WebRL Llama 3.1 8B

notes: The official Hub API resolves the former THUDM namespace to zai-org. Seven safetensors shards and configuration/tokenizer files are public and ungated. The card marks the weight license as other without naming complete terms, so no permissive weight license is inferred. name: WebRL outcome reward model 8B
summary: The outcome-supervision checkpoint used by WebRL to score browser trajectories during policy training.
notes: The official API resolves the former THUDM namespace to zai-org and lists four safetensors shards. No model card or weight-license declaration is present in the inspected manifest. The official WebRL README identifies this as its outcome-supervised reward model; it is a training component rather than an action policy.

name: Plan-and-Act Planner 70B

notes: The Hub manifest contains 17 safetensors shards and tokenizer/configuration files. These are recorded as publisher declarations, without claiming they override upstream model terms.

notes: Two safetensors shards and tokenizer/configuration files are publicly ungated. The model card declares MIT; upstream base-model terms are separate. The mutable card compares v1, v2 and UI-R1-E results without pinning every result to a commit, so this record identifies the Hub release and does not import an unversioned score.

name: UI-R1 3B training data

notes: The public manifest includes train.json and a train_imgs directory. The card has no dataset-license declaration, and the model’s MIT metadata is not inherited. The official repository identifies this as v1 training data drawn from AndroidControl and ScreenSpot; later enlarged training mixtures are distinct.

notes: The official Hub API resolves the former Reallm-Labs model namespace to InfiX-ai. Two safetensors shards and model/tokenizer files are public and ungated. The card declares Apache-2.0 for this checkpoint; base-model terms remain separate. Its older loading example still uses the prior namespace.

name: AgentCPM-GUI 8B checkpoint
summary: An eight-billion-parameter MiniCPM-V-based model that consumes smartphone screenshots and predicts compact actions for Chinese and English Android app tasks.
notes: The Hub provides four safetensors shards and associated model files without gating. Weight metadata declares Apache-2.0, while the prose license section refers specifically to code; these scopes are kept distinct. The card describes Android-app operation, and the CAGUI evaluation data remains a separate existing catalog asset.

name: POINTS-GUI-G 8B

notes: Four safetensors shards and model code/configuration are public and ungated. The card declares license other without specifying a named weight license. This release is the grounding model; the same card says the end-to-end GUI agent model is still under development. No end-to-end agent capability is inferred from grounding scores.
