name: Learning, Reasoning, Refinement: A Framework for Kahneman's Dual-System Intelligence in GUI Agents
summary: CogniGUI combines hierarchical visual parsing of interface elements with a GRPO-based grounding agent that compares alternative interaction paths. Its ScreenSeek benchmark evaluates navigation across applications, changing interface states, and consistency between interfaces.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Chain-of-Memory: Enhancing GUI Agents for Cross-Application Navigation
summary: Chain-of-Memory explicitly records action descriptions and task-relevant screen information in short- and long-term memory for GUI navigation. GUI Odyssey-CoM provides 111,000 screen-action pairs with memory annotations for learning and evaluating information retention across applications.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ZonUI-3B: A Lightweight Vision-Language Model for Cross-Resolution GUI Grounding
summary: ZonUI-3B trains GUI grounding with a curated 24,000-example collection of mobile, desktop, and web screenshots. Its two-stage procedure first learns across platforms and then specializes on high-resolution images, with ablations on data diversity and redundant examples.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: LineRetriever: Planning-Aware Observation Reduction for Web Agents
summary: LineRetriever uses a language model to select observation lines that matter for upcoming web-navigation actions. It reduces DOM or accessibility-tree context by considering the planning horizon instead of relying solely on semantic similarity.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: WebArxiv: A Reproducible Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Web Agents on arXiv Tasks
summary: WebArxiv provides 510 static-snapshot tasks with deterministic answers for scholarly browsing, including constrained paper retrieval, content extraction, and cross-paper comparison. The study also tests dynamic retrieval of interaction history to address repetitive or incomplete agent reasoning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Less is More: Empowering GUI Agent with Context-Aware Simplification
summary: SimpAgent prunes distracting interface elements with visual masks and compresses interaction history using consistency-based guidance. The study evaluates these two forms of context reduction during GUI navigation in web and mobile environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: How to Train Your LLM Web Agent: A Statistical Diagnosis
summary: Studies compute allocation for web-agent post-training with teacher-generated supervised fine-tuning followed by on-policy reinforcement learning. It samples 1,370 training configurations and uses bootstrap analysis to examine hyperparameter sensitivity on WorkArena and MiniWoB++.
verify_terms: How to Train Your LLM We
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: R-VLM: Region-Aware Vision Language Model for Precise GUI Grounding
summary: R-VLM localizes GUI elements through zoomed-in region proposals and an intersection-over-union-aware training objective. It evaluates the grounding model on ScreenSpot and AgentStudio and studies its effect on navigation in AITW and Mind2Web.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MobileGUI-RL: Advancing Mobile GUI Agent through Reinforcement Learning in Online Environment
summary: MobileGUI-RL constructs an online training curriculum through agent exploration and task filtering. It adapts GRPO with trajectory-aware advantages and rewards for task completion and execution efficiency, evaluated on three online mobile-agent benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GTA1: GUI Test-time Scaling Agent
summary: GTA1 samples multiple action proposals at each GUI step and uses a judge to select among them. A separate grounding model is trained with reinforcement learning to map selected proposals to visual targets, linking planning-time search with click localization.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-G$^2$: Gaussian Reward Modeling for GUI Grounding
summary: GUI-G2 replaces binary grounding rewards with Gaussian point rewards and spatial-coverage rewards. An adaptive variance tied to element dimensions supplies continuous training feedback for targets of different sizes, evaluated on the ScreenSpot benchmark family.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MobileUse: A GUI Agent with Hierarchical Reflection for Autonomous Mobile Operation
summary: MobileUse reflects on errors at action and task timescales, invoking reflection when needed and using proactive exploration to learn unfamiliar apps. It evaluates this mobile execution framework on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab and describes a toolkit for physical-device operation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: OS-MAP: How Far Can Computer-Using Agents Go in Breadth and Depth?
summary: OS-MAP organizes 416 computer-use tasks across 15 applications by a five-level automation taxonomy and a hierarchy of user demands. The benchmark separates required autonomy from generalization scope to diagnose where agents struggle as task demands increase.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MMBench-GUI: Hierarchical Multi-Platform Evaluation Framework for GUI Agents
summary: MMBench-GUI evaluates interface understanding, element grounding, task automation, and collaboration across six named desktop, mobile, and web platforms. It introduces the Efficiency-Quality Area metric for examining execution efficiency alongside task quality in online GUI automation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Magentic-UI: Towards Human-in-the-loop Agentic Systems
summary: Magentic-UI combines browser interaction, code execution, file operations, and MCP tools in an interface for human-agent collaboration. It studies collaborative planning and task execution, action guards, and persistent memory through benchmark tasks, simulated users, user studies, and safety assessments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: NaturalGAIA: A Verifiable Benchmark and Hierarchical Framework for Long-Horizon GUI Tasks
summary: NaturalGAIA builds verifiable long-horizon GUI tasks from human interaction intents while separating causal task structure from its verbal description. Its LightManus-Jarvis framework divides dynamic planning and context management from execution based on visual and structural interface information.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CoAct-1: Computer-using Multi-Agent System with Coding Actions
summary: CoAct-1 delegates subtasks between a GUI operator and a programmer that executes Python or Bash. Its OSWorld evaluation studies a hybrid action space in which scripts handle suitable file and data operations while visual interaction handles other steps.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Uncertainty-Aware GUI Agent: Adaptive Perception through Component Recommendation and Human-in-the-Loop Refinement
summary: RecAgent narrows attention to recommended UI components and requests user feedback when task intent or decisions remain uncertain. It introduces ComplexAction to evaluate specified single-step GUI actions in difficult interface scenarios.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Evolving in Tasks: Empowering the Multi-modality Large Language Model as the Computer Use Agent
summary: The Self-Evolution Agent combines automatic generation of verifiable computer-use trajectories with step-wise reinforcement learning for long-horizon training. It also describes a model-enhancement procedure that integrates grounding and planning capabilities without an additional training stage.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Beyond Pixels: Exploring DOM Downsampling for LLM-Based Web Agents
summary: D2Snap reduces serialized DOM observations while preserving actionable elements and features that distinguish their uses. The study compares reduced DOM inputs with screenshot-based observations for a web agent on tasks sampled from Online-Mind2Web.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SEAgent: Self-Evolving Computer Use Agent with Autonomous Learning from Experience
summary: SEAgent explores unfamiliar software using a world-state assessor and an automatically generated task curriculum. It learns from failed and successful interactions through adversarial imitation and GRPO, then combines specialist experience into a generalist agent evaluated on five OSWorld software environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Test-Time Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding via Region Consistency
summary: GUI-RC aggregates multiple grounding predictions into spatial voting grids to choose a consensus region. GUI-RCPO then turns agreement with that region into a reward for test-time policy updates on unlabeled GUI screenshots.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: FineState-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Fine-Grained State Control in GUI Agents
summary: FineState-Bench evaluates fine-grained GUI perception and control across desktop, web, and mobile interfaces. Its Visual Diagnostic Assistant separates perception and localization contributions in controlled interaction experiments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CRAFT-GUI: Curriculum-Reinforced Agent For GUI Tasks
summary: CRAFT-GUI organizes GUI trajectories by difficulty for curriculum-based GRPO training. Its reward combines rule-based signals with model judgments, with evaluation on Android Control and an internal online benchmark.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: WebMall -- A Multi-Shop Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents
summary: WebMall provides four simulated online shops with heterogeneous product data for comparison shopping, related-product searches, and checkout tasks. It evaluates web agents with different observation formats and memory configurations in a fixed offline environment.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: V2P: Visual Attention Calibration for GUI Grounding via Background Suppression and Center Peaking
summary: V2P trains GUI grounding by suppressing attention to background regions and emphasizing the center of the target element. It represents target importance with size-dependent Gaussian heatmaps and evaluates the contribution of each component on ScreenSpot-v2 and ScreenSpot-Pro.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CODA: Coordinating the Cerebrum and Cerebellum for a Dual-Brain Computer Use Agent with Decoupled Reinforcement Learning
summary: CODA combines a generalist planner with a specialist GUI executor and trains application-specific planners through decoupled GRPO. Successful specialist trajectories then support supervised training of a consolidated planner, evaluated across four ScienceBoard applications.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: You Don't Know Until You Click:Automated GUI Testing for Production-Ready Software Evaluation
summary: RealDevWorld evaluates generated software repositories with 194 development tasks and AppEvalPilot, an agent judge that operates the resulting GUIs. The evaluation examines functional behavior, visual fidelity, and runtime responses to produce task-specific diagnostic feedback.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: A Functionality-Grounded Benchmark for Evaluating Web Agents in E-commerce Domains
summary: Amazon-Bench generates functionality-specific web tasks from page content and interactive controls, covering operations beyond product search. Its evaluator checks task completion and unintended changes to account state, such as address or purchase settings.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: WebSight: A Vision-First Architecture for Robust Web Agents
summary: WebSight uses a vision-language model trained on web-interface examples within a modular agent with planning, action, verification, and episodic memory components. It evaluates element clicking on Showdown Clicks and full browsing tasks on WebVoyager using visual observations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UItron: Foundational GUI Agent with Advanced Perception and Planning
summary: UItron combines GUI perception and planning data engineering with supervised training and curriculum reinforcement learning in connected mobile and PC environments. It also collects more than one million operation steps across 100 Chinese apps and builds offline and online evaluation environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: KG-RAG: Enhancing GUI Agent Decision-Making via Knowledge Graph-Driven Retrieval-Augmented Generation
summary: KG-RAG converts UI transition graphs into a searchable vector store and uses intent-guided retrieval to construct actionable navigation paths. It introduces KG-Android-Bench and KG-Harmony-Bench and evaluates transfer from mobile apps to web and desktop tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: FlashAdventure: A Benchmark for GUI Agents Solving Full Story Arcs in Diverse Adventure Games
summary: FlashAdventure evaluates GUI agents on completing story arcs in 34 adventure games. It pairs an automated gameplay judge with COAST, a framework that keeps long-term clue memory to plan and complete sequential objectives.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Succeed or Learn Slowly: Sample Efficient Off-Policy Reinforcement Learning for Mobile App Control
summary: Succeed or Learn Slowly applies direct off-policy updates to successful interactions and more conservative regularized updates to negative examples. Successful Transition Replay prioritizes successful experience during policy learning, with evaluation on AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UI-TARS-2 Technical Report: Advancing GUI Agent with Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
summary: UI-TARS-2 combines scalable trajectory generation, stabilized multi-turn reinforcement learning, and a sandbox that supports GUI, filesystem, and terminal actions. The report evaluates the resulting agent across web, desktop, Android, and game tasks and analyzes training stability.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Learning Active Perception via Self-Evolving Preference Optimization for GUI Grounding
summary: LASER builds preference data for multi-step GUI perception by combining Monte Carlo quality estimates with region-overlap evaluation. Its self-evolving training encourages relevant region selection and adapts the amount of reasoning before predicting screen coordinates.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MAS-Bench: A Unified Benchmark for Shortcut-Augmented Hybrid Mobile GUI Agents
summary: MAS-Bench evaluates mobile agents that combine GUI actions with APIs, deep links, and reusable scripts. Its 139 tasks across 11 apps test use of 88 predefined shortcuts as well as the ability to generate new reusable workflows.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: MobileRL: Online Agentic Reinforcement Learning for Mobile GUI Agents
summary: MobileRL adapts GRPO to mobile GUI training with difficulty-dependent replay of successes and filtering of failure curricula. A shortest-path reward adjustment accounts for task length, with evaluations on AndroidWorld and AndroidLab.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UI-S1: Advancing GUI Automation via Semi-online Reinforcement Learning
summary: UI-S1 simulates multi-turn online learning over offline trajectories, using a patch module to recover divergences while retaining the model’s own outputs in context. It combines discounted future returns with step- and episode-level advantages and introduces a semi-online performance proxy.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: How Auxiliary Reasoning Unleashes GUI Grounding in VLMs
summary: Studies the gap between latent visual grounding and explicit coordinate output in general vision-language models. Three zero-shot methods add axes, grids, or labeled intersections to GUI screenshots so models can express spatial locations without fine-tuning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: TGPO: Tree-Guided Preference Optimization for Robust Web Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: TGPO merges semantically equivalent web states into tree-structured trajectories for offline preference optimization. A process reward model scores subgoal progress, redundant behavior, and action validity, while dynamic weighting emphasizes consequential decisions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Detecting Pipeline Failures through Fine-Grained Analysis of Web Agents
summary: Introduces a modular framework for identifying errors at intermediate stages of a web-agent pipeline. A SeeAct and Mind2Web case study examines weaknesses that are obscured by final task-success metrics.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-ReWalk: Massive Data Generation for GUI Agent via Stochastic Exploration and Intent-Aware Reasoning
summary: GUI-ReWalk begins with stochastic interface exploration and then infers goals to generate coherent action trajectories. It supports long-horizon workflows across applications and studies training on the resulting data using grounding and navigation benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UIPro: Unleashing Superior Interaction Capability For GUI Agents
summary: UIPro pretrains GUI understanding on 20.6 million tasks and then harmonizes interaction datasets through a unified action space. Continued fine-tuning uses the merged multi-platform data to train action prediction for generalist GUI operation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-ARP: Enhancing Grounding with Adaptive Region Perception for GUI Agents
summary: GUI-ARP uses visual attention to crop relevant screenshot regions and decides whether a target needs single-stage or multi-stage analysis. Supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO trains this adaptive procedure for high-resolution GUI grounding.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Orcust: Stepwise-Feedback Reinforcement Learning for GUI Agent
summary: Orcust combines principle-constrained reward modeling with GUI trajectory collection in instrumented virtual machines. Environment-checkable and model-derived principles guide stepwise feedback for grounding, basic operations, and complete task execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Efficient Multi-turn RL for GUI Agents via Decoupled Training and Adaptive Data Curation
summary: DART separates GUI reinforcement learning into asynchronous environment, rollout, data-management, and training services. It curates experience by task difficulty, successful trajectories, and step uncertainty while correcting rollout-policy mismatch, with evaluation on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Scaling Synthetic Task Generation for Agents via Exploration
summary: AutoPlay explores application states and functions to generate tasks, then uses a model executor and verifier to construct demonstrations. It produces 20,000 tasks across 20 Android apps and 10,000 tasks across 13 Ubuntu apps for supervised and reinforcement learning of UI agents.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SCUBA: Salesforce Computer Use Benchmark
summary: SCUBA evaluates enterprise UI navigation and CRM workflows with 300 task instances derived from Salesforce user interviews. Salesforce sandbox execution and milestone-based assessment support comparisons between zero-shot agents and agents given demonstrations.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Ferret-UI Lite: Lessons from Building Small On-Device GUI Agents
summary: Ferret-UI Lite develops a 3B GUI agent using mixed real and synthetic data, reasoning with visual tools at inference, and reinforcement learning. It evaluates grounding and navigation across mobile, web, and desktop settings, including AndroidWorld and OSWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Before Acting, Change the State: Prospective State Intervention for Web Agents under Deceptive Interfaces
summary: Introduces Veer, a runtime defense that changes task-relevant web state when an otherwise valid proposed action would produce an unauthorized consequence. It plans a prospective intervention and grounds and verifies its execution before the base agent continues.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: PhoneCLI: From App Interfaces to Callable Commands for Mobile Agents
summary: Introduces PhoneCLI, which explores mobile app interfaces and compiles navigation paths into reusable commands without internal app APIs or instrumentation. At execution time it verifies compiled paths and falls back to a visual agent for open-ended interaction or failed navigation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Structured Interaction, Visual Localization, and Robust Execution for Complex Web Tasks: A Technical Report on the WebRetriever Challenge
summary: Describes a WebRetriever agent that combines semantic webpage operations with visual localization when structured representations are insufficient. Hierarchical context management and fault-aware execution support processing tasks across concurrent browsers.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SCOUT: Synergizing Reasoning and Tool-Use for Computer-Use Safety
summary: Introduces SCOUT, a safety verifier that first derives task-specific completion and safety rubrics from a computer-use trajectory, then actively probes the resulting environment for evidence. It evaluates whether these two stages detect harmful consequences that screenshots alone can miss.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Relevance Does Not Imply Applicability: Experience Activation for Personal GUI Agents
summary: Introduces ExpActivator, which matches the current GUI state to relevant historical states before supplying past actions as guidance. A separate activation rule decides whether a recurring user intent is warranted by the current time and situation or should be withheld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Probe to Act: Elevating Browser-Use Agent via Active Visual Probing
summary: Introduces Probe to Act, which lets browser agents request visual evidence linking DOM handles and screen regions before committing an operation. It retains selected interaction evidence as memory and studies both prompted use and distillation into open models.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: REBASE: Device-Cloud Experience Coherence for GUI Agents Across App Updates
summary: Introduces REBASE, a device–cloud protocol for repairing cached GUI experience after app updates. It combines cloud replay, device-side step verification, and progressively richer failure reports to produce repairs tied to application versions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: PastForward: Faster On-Device GUI Agents via Computational Experience Reuse
summary: Introduces PastForward, which reuses earlier output sequences as verified decoding proposals and starts future action computation from predicted GUI transitions. Screen checks determine whether speculative computation and cached model states can be retained.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: From Trajectories to Grounded Preferences: Process Preference Synthesis via Interaction Element Graphs for Web PRMs
summary: Introduces SURFPRM, which turns web demonstrations into an interaction-element graph for synthesizing grounded negative actions. Its contrastive preference data trains process reward models to distinguish plausible on-page alternatives and guide downstream trajectory search.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CUA-SWE: When Computer-Use Agents Meet Visual Software Engineering
summary: Introduces CUA-SWE, a benchmark and execution environment that combines code changes with graphical interaction and visual inspection of running software. Task-specific tests verify repairs and changes whose required information may be available only through the application interface.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: The GUI Is Not the State: Diagnosing State Aliasing in GUI World Models
summary: Introduces StateAliasBench to isolate GUI world-model ambiguities in which matching visible screens and actions can lead to different futures. It augments frozen world models with structured state recovered from interaction history and evaluates the effect on prediction and agent execution.
verify_terms: The GUI Is Not the State
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CUA-Sandbox: Efficient Environments for Computer-Use Agent Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces CUA-Sandbox, which separates each rollout’s mutable state from shared initialized software runtimes. State-scoped execution and transactional resets or branches aim to reduce training-environment costs while retaining original interfaces and evaluators.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: AgentTell: Behavioural Side-Channel Leakage in Browser-Use Agents
summary: Introduces AgentTell, a benchmark for privacy leakage through browser actions after an agent learns a private fact on another website. It examines whether agents choose revealing options despite nondisclosure instructions and whether their final reports accurately describe that behavior.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CaptchaArena: A Large-Scale, Fine-Grained Dataset for Training Computer-Use Agents on Interactive CAPTCHAs
summary: Introduces CaptchaArena, a dataset of execution-verified interactive CAPTCHA solutions with screenshot–action trajectories, reasoning annotations, and pixel masks for irregular targets. The work trains a single policy across CAPTCHA types using supervised learning followed by verifier-reward reinforcement learning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CAVEAT: Towards Robust Computer-Use Agents in Incentive-Misaligned Environments
summary: Introduces CAVEAT, a controlled marketplace benchmark for testing whether delegated agents preserve user objectives when interfaces favor other outcomes. It diagnoses decision failures and studies harness interventions and targeted training to improve resistance to marketplace steering.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SIR: Self-improving Red-teaming for Compute Use Agents
summary: Introduces SIR, which iteratively refines a reusable library of prompt-injection strategies from failed computer-use attack trajectories. Its evaluation uses deterministic system-state checks and counts attacks only when the adversarial objective and legitimate task both complete.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SCAFFOLD: Self-Improving Web Agents via Recursive Parametric Skill Abstraction
summary: Introduces SCAFFOLD, which extracts executable skills from web trajectories, composes them into a hierarchy, and compresses redundant skills through behavioral checks. It periodically distills skill-guided trajectories into the policy and studies repeated improvement across web benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: When and What to Teach: Budget-Aware Online Adaptation for Web Agents
summary: Proposes an online teaching framework that decides which web-agent episodes warrant a stronger teacher and which trajectory turns merit training. A solvability gate and score-guided trimming aim to preserve first-attempt performance while reducing teaching and training costs.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ActReal: System-Level Mobile Agents Challenge Mobile Automation Detection
summary: Introduces ActReal, which translates semantic mobile-agent actions into coordinated touch and sensor signals to study automation-detection weaknesses. It evaluates detectors that observe touch events alone or together with inertial measurements under a privileged executor threat model.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-CC: Benchmarking Contextual Consistency of GUI World Models as Agent Environments
summary: Introduces GUI-CC, a benchmark for assessing GUI world models as multi-step agent environments. Separate reference-action and agent-loop tracks test whether generated screens preserve context, plausible transitions, and task progress throughout interaction.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Learning Simple Test-Time Environments for LLM Web Agents
summary: Introduces Test-Time Environment Decomposition, which uses trial interaction to break complex web observations into simpler modules. A label-free adaptation procedure learns from these sub-environments and studies whether their gains compose in full web tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CURA: Certified Runtime Alarms for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces CURA, a telemetry-based runtime monitor that turns computer-use trajectories into sequential failure alarms and can trigger mid-task oversight. Its certificate controls false alarms, while the study separately reports detection performance and limits of retrospective monitoring.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Iron: Intent-Aligned and Retrospective Dual Learning Framework for Enhancing Generalist Virtual Agents
summary: Introduces Iron, a GUI-agent training framework that aligns low-level actions with high-level intent using cycle-consistency rewards. It also repurposes failed trajectories through hindsight reconstruction and evaluates transfer to other digital tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Beyond Task Completion: Training Capable and Safe Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces SCOPE, which trains computer-use agents on ordinary task demonstrations, safe continuations around hazards, and explicit refusals. Its SCOPE-Gen pipeline pairs verifiable tasks with environmental-risk variants to support joint capability and safety training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: LocalLSTC: A Long Short-Term Control Architecture for Locally Deployed GUI Agents
summary: Introduces LocalLSTC, a training-free control architecture that maintains persistent task state and uses it to form short execution commitments. Outcomes feed back into that state for progress checks, recovery, and termination in locally deployed desktop agents.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Reflection with Action-Induced Visual Differences for Desktop GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Evidence-First Reflection, which separates extraction of action-induced screen changes from judgment of whether an operation achieved its objective. It filters visual differences into relevant evidence before a desktop agent’s reflector decides how execution should continue.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: WebMCP-Phalanx: Enforcing and Characterizing Trust Boundaries for Browser-Integrated LLM Agents
summary: Proposes WebMCP-Phalanx, a browser-integrated runtime that binds page-exposed tools to their registering principals and separates content inspection from privileged invocation. It studies lifecycle and prompt-injection attacks, including a timing bypass that motivates validating all visible metadata before tool use.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Are Android GUI Agents Robust Against Runtime Anomalies? AnTrap: Evaluating Agents in Dynamic Adversarial Environments
summary: Introduces AnTrap, which injects task-solvable runtime anomalies into Android GUI-agent trajectories using a layered failure taxonomy. It compares model robustness and adversarial reinforcement learning to distinguish recoverable interface traps from persistent contextual failures.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Task-Adaptive Rubrics for GUI Reward Modeling
summary: Introduces AdaptRubric, which retrieves reusable criteria for a GUI task family and then generates instruction-specific checks for concrete values and constraints. It evaluates these adaptive rubrics in offline reward assessment and online agent optimization.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: BrowserForge: Scaling Web Episode via Parallel Browser Sandboxes
summary: Introduces BrowserForge, which combines broad website sourcing, parallel browser sandboxes, and task-proposer/solver interaction to collect verified web trajectories. The pipeline uses page structure during synthesis but trains a policy that acts from screenshots.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GSAR: Goal-State-Anchor Rewards for Mobile GUI Agents with Self-Evolving Data Synthesis
summary: Introduces GSAR, which synthesizes GUI tasks and successful goal states, then annotates task-relevant interface elements as reward anchors. These anchors support offline trajectory verification and online policy training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: CausalCache: Conditional High-Fidelity Restoration for Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: Introduces CausalCache, which selects archived screenshots to restore alongside text summaries under a fixed visual-memory budget. A history-gated adapter processes restored images, with evaluation distinguishing standard step limits from longer-horizon and mobile-transfer settings.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Beyond Success and Failure: Length-Aware Contrastive Learning for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces LACL-GUI, a contrastive learning objective that distinguishes trajectory quality within both successful and failed GUI executions. It favors concise successes and uses divergence from successful trajectories to differentiate failures during policy optimization.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: GUI-Primitives: Diagnosing Spatial Reasoning Failures in Vision-Language GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces GUI-Primitives, a paired-instruction benchmark that changes a spatial relation while holding the screenshot and anchor fixed. Its diagnostics separate failure to localize either candidate from failure to choose the candidate satisfying the relation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Lexical Coupling in GUI Element Grounding: Sentence Embeddings Track Labels across Mobile and Web
summary: Studies whether text-embedding GUI grounding scores reflect semantic matching or recovery of visible labels. Same-screen ranking comparisons with lexical baselines expose differences between deployable fusion, oracle selection, and performance on label-poor targets.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Echoverse: Deep, Evolving Environments for Training Computer-Use Agents at Scale
summary: Introduces Echoverse, which compiles specifications into stateful applications with database-grounded graders and uses rollouts to improve both the environments and agent policies. It examines behavioral depth, targeted interface practice, and environment repair as sources of training value.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: How Benchmarks Mis-Score Computer-Use Agents
summary: Audits failure-scored computer-use trajectories to distinguish agent errors from broken tasks and evaluator false negatives. It organizes reliability issues across task construction, trajectory evidence, scoring, and reporting, then derives corresponding evaluation design practices.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Why Are GUI Agents Correct but Late? Decode on the Decision-Time Critical Path, Tested with Pre-Compiled Policy Trees
summary: Introduces Adaptive Anticipatory Policy Trees, which precompute guarded actions and deadlines during idle periods so transient GUI events can be handled without new text generation. Paired experiments examine when this prepared execution helps and when reactive control remains preferable.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Rethinking Inference-Time Scaling in Local Computer-Use Agents: Failure Modes and Compute Tradeoffs
summary: Examines inference-time scaling for local computer-use models by varying context, step budgets, decomposition, and parallel execution. OSWorld experiments track both task performance and changing failure modes, exposing cases where extra computation extends errors or adds coordination overhead.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: OSReward: Instituting Standardized Evaluation for Cross-Platform Computer-Use Reward Models
summary: Introduces OSReward and its harder and multidimensional variants for assessing judgments of computer-use trajectories. It also releases a reasoning-annotated judgment corpus and trains reward models, examining reliability, leniency bias, and evaluation cost.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Interactive Reward Agent: GUI Task Evaluation via Environment-State Verification
summary: Introduces an Interactive Reward Agent that proposes completion conditions and verifies them using system, application, and GUI tools after execution. GUI-RewardBench provides annotated desktop trajectories for evaluating these evidence-based judgments and their use in reinforcement learning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Desktop-Delta Bench: Do Computer-Use Models Understand Desktop GUI Transitions?
summary: Introduces Desktop-Delta Bench, an offline diagnostic of GUI transition understanding using temporal-ordering tasks and before/after action inference. It includes decoy observations to test whether models track the source and task relevance of screen changes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Scaling GUI Agents with Visual State Transitions
summary: Introduces State Transition Pretraining, which jointly learns to infer actions from GUI changes and predict future states from current screens and actions. Subsequent instruction-trajectory fine-tuning tests whether these representations transfer to desktop and mobile agent tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Falsifiable Commitment Planning for Self-Correcting Web Agents
summary: Introduces FCPAgent, which attaches confirming and falsifying evidence to each skill-grounded plan step. A plan–test–repair loop checks actions and observations, then localizes contradictions so execution, skills, or plans can be revised at the appropriate level.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SeekJudge: A Practical Reward Framework for Reinforcement Learning in Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces SeekJudge, which iteratively searches and analyzes GUI trajectories to assess instruction fulfillment. The work combines dense judgment-data synthesis, a step-label benchmark, and reward-server scheduling to study accurate and practical reward feedback for agent training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: StateAct: Program State, before Pixels, for Long-Horizon Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces StateAct, a code-first computer-use harness that manipulates program state directly and delegates screenshot-and-click subgoals to a GUI agent. An independent completion gate checks saved outputs, while fresh subagents handle subgoals to limit accumulated context.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: Sidekick: Designing Communication for Effective Multitasking with Computer Use Agents
summary: Introduces Sidekick, a communication interface that uses ambient status cues, multimodal action summaries, and visual and verbal explanations of reasoning to help people monitor computer-use agents. A user study examines progress awareness, error traceability, and multitasking across background and foreground interaction.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: SEE: Structure-aware Exploring & Exploiting for Long-horizon GUI Agent Trajectory Synthesis
summary: Introduces SEE, which first explores mobile interfaces to build a screen-and-element transition graph, then composes task trajectories through graph planning and controlled sampling. It studies coverage, loop avoidance, and transfer after training agents on the generated sequences.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: EvoGUI: An Evolution-Aware Benchmark for GUI State-Transition Understanding
summary: Introduces EvoGUI, which derives temporal ordering, inverse action/value prediction, and successor-discrimination probes from recorded GUI trajectories. Its web-derived benchmark isolates transition understanding from the other abilities involved in end-to-end task success.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: UI-MOPD: Multi-Platform On-Policy Distillation for Unified GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Uni-GUI, a collection of executable desktop and mobile trajectories, and UI-MOPD, which trains a shared policy from its own rollouts using platform-specific teachers. The distillation procedure routes each visited state to the appropriate teacher to preserve distinct interaction conventions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the primary paper abstract.

name: ShowUI-web
summary: Web-interface grounding examples with instructions, element boxes and points, paired with a separately packaged screenshot archive.

name: OpenCUA 32B
summary: A Qwen2.5-VL-based computer-use checkpoint that combines screenshot history with planning and grounded executable actions.
notes: The public manifest contains 64 safetensors shards. The card declares MIT for this model and names its Qwen2.5-VL base; upstream terms remain separate. This is the 32B release, distinct from the existing 72B preview. Family-level or 72B benchmark scores are not transferred to it.

name: CogAgent 9B 20241220
summary: A bilingual GLM-4V-based execution model that uses screenshots, task instructions and action history to predict GUI operations.
notes: The former THUDM model URL resolves to zai-org. Six public safetensors shards are present. Weights use the custom CogAgent License, including a registration requirement for commercial use, rather than a blanket permissive license. The card cites the 2023 CogAgent paper as previous work and links a later technical report; no claim that the old paper documents this 2024 checkpoint is asserted.

name: InfiGUI-G1 7B

notes: Four safetensors shards are public. The model card declares Apache-2.0 and identifies Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct as its base. It is the G1 grounding checkpoint, distinct from the previously cataloged InfiGUI-R1 reasoning checkpoint; benchmark scores remain publisher claims.

name: GUI-G2 7B
summary: A Qwen2.5-VL grounding checkpoint trained with Gaussian point and coverage rewards whose granularity adapts to interface-element scale.
notes: The model card and four public safetensors shards establish this specific release. Apache-2.0 is declared for the model. The release targets element grounding; its grounding results do not establish long-horizon task-completion success.

name: UI-AGILE checkpoint
summary: The released UI-AGILE model for GUI grounding with reward shaping, crop-based resampling and decomposed selection during inference.
notes: Four safetensors shards and model/tokenizer files are public. The card declares MIT for these weights; the companion dataset has no declared license and is separate. The short card does not state a parameter count, so this entry does not infer one from shard sizes.

name: Aria-UI context-aware checkpoint
summary: The context-aware Aria-UI release that uses interaction context to support grounding in dynamic Android and desktop agent tasks.
notes: The Hub manifest exposes twelve safetensors shards and model code/configuration, but no README card or model-license declaration. The official repository explicitly announces this context-aware release separately from the base model. Code or base-model licenses are not inherited.

name: GUI-R1 checkpoint bundle
summary: A single Hub release containing GUI-R1 3B and 7B action-model checkpoints trained with reinforcement learning across interface platforms.
notes: The manifest contains two safetensors shards in GUI-R1-3B and four in GUI-R1-7B. Both are counted as one Hub resource rather than duplicate root URLs. The model card declares MIT; this does not automatically apply to source training data or upstream base models.

name: GUI-G1 3B v1
summary: A Qwen2.5-VL-3B checkpoint released for R1-style visual grounding experiments, predicting interface target locations from screenshots and instructions.
notes: Two public safetensors shards and model/tokenizer configuration are present. The card declares MIT. Its inference example loads the v1 model but names a different 0.1K processor checkpoint; that example was not executed, and compatibility is not asserted.

name: SkillWeaver
summary: A web-agent framework that explores sites, synthesizes reusable interaction APIs and builds a skill library for later tasks.
notes: Exploration, task execution, browser integration and evaluation code are published under MIT. Synthesized skill files are included, but no trained model weights are implied. The source depends on external web environments and model services; no runtime or browser tasks were executed.

name: RedTeamCUA
summary: A controlled testing framework that combines desktop virtual machines and replicated websites to evaluate computer-use agents against indirect prompt injection.
notes: The release includes environment code, adversarial scenario configuration and RTC-Bench task-generation assets. The project declares Apache-2.0, while incorporated environments retain their licenses. It distinguishes full task runs from tests initialized at injection locations; those settings must not be treated as interchangeable results.

name: Web-Shepherd inference and evaluation
summary: Process-reward inference and benchmark-evaluation utilities that use task checklists to assess individual web-agent decisions.
notes: The tree contains src/webprm modules and a WebRewardBench evaluation script. The README’s illustrative folder layout differs from the actual tree, so a complete training pipeline is not claimed. No root code license is declared. Some old checkpoint links are unavailable; current model releases are separately identified through the official Hub collection.

name: Go-Browse
summary: Structured website-exploration and data-processing code that revisits discovered pages, proposes tasks and collects trajectories for web-agent fine-tuning.
notes: The release contains exploration agents, data-processing scripts, fine-tuning and WebArena evaluation entry points under MIT. Checkpoints and processed datasets are separate Hub resources with separate license status. The arXiv badge image has an unrelated number; the linked paper and citation consistently identify 2506.03533.

name: ShowUI-π checkpoint
summary: A compact visual-action checkpoint that predicts continuous GUI drag trajectories from a screenshot and a natural-language instruction.
notes: A model.safetensors file and policy pre/postprocessor configuration are publicly ungated. The card describes a SmolVLA-based GUI drag-and-drop model despite its generic robotics pipeline tag. No weight-license declaration or specific operating-system coverage is provided.

name: Holo1 7B
summary: A Qwen2.5-VL-based action model released for the Surfer-H web-agent system, supporting policy, interface-localization and validation roles.
notes: Four public safetensors shards and example navigation/localization files are present. The model card declares Apache-2.0. Reported Surfer-H results depend on the assembled policy/localizer/validator configuration and are not imported as standalone checkpoint scores.

name: ScaleCUA 7B
summary: A Qwen2.5-VL-based computer-use checkpoint with direct grounding and agent action modes across desktop, mobile and web interfaces.
notes: Four public safetensors shards and model/tokenizer configuration are present. The card declares Apache-2.0. The model card’s Paper link points to the code repository, so the arXiv association uses the repository’s explicit citation rather than treating that link as a paper URL.

name: WebShepherd 3B
summary: A public text-based process-reward checkpoint from the Web-Shepherd collection for scoring web-agent decisions against task checklists.
notes: The official project-linked collection identifies this public 3B checkpoint. The README uses a separate unavailable WebShepherd/web-shepherd-base URL; redirect equivalence is not asserted. Two safetensors shards and a Qwen2 causal-language-model configuration are present. No model card or weight license is published in the inspected manifest. The separately announced multimodal 3B model is not assumed released.

name: Go-Browse WebArena Qwen 7B
summary: A Qwen-2.5-7B-Instruct checkpoint fine-tuned on Go-Browse WebArena trajectories for website task execution.
notes: Seven public safetensors shards and model/tokenizer files are present. The card links the official code and paper but declares no weight license. The code repository’s MIT license is not inherited by this checkpoint, and the separate NNetNav-trained comparison model is not treated as an alias.

name: Go-Browse-WA processed data
summary: Flattened web-interaction training records with accessibility-tree observations, assistant completions, trajectory rewards and step-link metadata.
notes: The public release contains nine Parquet shards. The short card supplies schema and split metadata but no license declaration; the official README describes successful and unsuccessful trajectories processed for fine-tuning. The raw screenshot/HTML corpus is a separate release and is not claimed to be included here.

dataset_profile.notes: The card count is flattened step records, not trajectories or independent tasks. Both successful and unsuccessful trajectories are included according to the project README; no license is declared.

name: WebPRM Collection preference data
summary: Checklist-annotated web decision records with page observations, prior actions, one preferred continuation and rejected alternatives for process-reward learning.
notes: Ten public Parquet shards are present. The card names its split test and reports 9,460 rows; the project’s 40K-plus preference-annotation claim is a different grain and is not substituted for this row count. A row can contain multiple rejected alternatives. No data-license declaration is present.

dataset_profile.notes: Preserves the publisher’s split label despite the collection’s training purpose. Rows are not individual preference pairs because rejected is a list. Data license is unknown.

name: WebRewardBench
summary: An offline preference-evaluation set for web process reward models, pairing page and trajectory context with preferred and rejected candidate decisions.
notes: Two public Parquet shards are present. Card metadata reports 776 test rows, whereas the project describes 1,000-plus test cases without reconciling that count to rows. Both observations are retained as a grain/coverage caveat rather than treating either as a confirmed number of independent tasks. No data license is declared.

benchmark_protocol.evaluation: Compare reward-model preferences with the provided chosen/rejected decision labels; no independent score was reproduced.
benchmark_protocol.notes: The current Hub row count and project case-count claim use unresolved counting units. Candidate lists mean a row must not be assumed to equal one task or one pair.

name: ActionBert: Leveraging User Actions for Semantic Understanding of User Interfaces
summary: Pretrains ActionBert on user interaction traces to combine visual, linguistic, and UI-structure features. It evaluates the resulting UI representations on tasks including icon classification and description-based component retrieval.

name: Understanding Mobile GUI: from Pixel-Words to Screen-Sentences
summary: Models mobile screens as atomic text and graphic components whose relationships are learned by a Screen Transformer. The work introduces RICO-PW annotations and evaluates metadata-free screen understanding on relation, clickability, retrieval, and app-classification tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: Learning to Denoise Raw Mobile UI Layouts for Improving Datasets at Scale
summary: Introduces CLAY, a pipeline that repairs noisy mobile UI layouts by removing nodes without valid visual counterparts and assigning semantic element types, supported by human-annotated layouts for evaluation.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot.

name: Enabling Conversational Interaction with Mobile UI using Large Language Models
summary: Studies few-shot prompting of a single language model for four mobile-UI interaction tasks, aiming to support conversational interface use without a separate trained model for each task.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Spotlight: Mobile UI Understanding using Vision-Language Models with a Focus
summary: Introduces Spotlight, a vision-language model conditioned on a UI screenshot and a selected region of interest. It evaluates screenshot-based mobile UI understanding and explores multitask learning and few-shot prompting.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Towards Better Semantic Understanding of Mobile Interfaces
summary: Augments RICO screens and view hierarchies with human labels for icon shape and meaning and for links between UI elements and text labels. It compares image-only and multimodal models on semantic understanding of previously unseen apps.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Lexi: Self-Supervised Learning of the UI Language
summary: Introduces Lexi and UICaption to learn UI image-text representations from descriptions of interface functionality. Evaluation covers UI action entailment, instruction-based retrieval, referring-expression grounding, and UI entity recognition.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Language Models can Solve Computer Tasks
summary: Introduces recursive criticism and improvement prompting for language-model agents performing computer tasks, evaluated on MiniWoB++ with a small number of demonstrations per task.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Multimodal Web Navigation with Instruction-Finetuned Foundation Models
summary: Trains WebGUM offline from demonstrations by jointly tuning an instruction-following language model and a vision encoder over webpage screenshots and HTML. The agent predicts browser actions and is evaluated on MiniWoB, WebShop, and Mind2Web.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Hierarchical Prompting Assists Large Language Model on Web Navigation
summary: Separates web navigation prompting into a SUMMARIZER that extracts action-relevant observations and an ACTOR that chooses the next action from the condensed context.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: From Pixels to UI Actions: Learning to Follow Instructions via Graphical User Interfaces
summary: Studies instruction-following agents that observe screenshots and act through a generic mouse-and-keyboard action space, evaluating pixel-based pretraining for GUI tasks on MiniWoB++.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: InstructExcel: A Benchmark for Natural Language Instruction in Excel
summary: Introduces InstructExcel, a benchmark for generating Excel OfficeScripts from natural-language requests, built using scripts recorded from user actions and a collection of existing spreadsheets.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its normalized abstract SHA-256 matches the retained bibliographic snapshot. This is an application-specific automation benchmark grounded in recorded Excel user actions. Its execution interface is OfficeScripts, so it is adjacent rather than a visual GUI navigation benchmark.

name: Explore, Select, Derive, and Recall: Augmenting LLM with Human-like Memory for Mobile Task Automation
summary: Introduces MobileGPT, which organizes mobile-app experience into reusable subtasks using an explore, select, derive, and recall cycle. Its memory supports learning task procedures and adapting them to new contexts.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AgentBoard: An Analytical Evaluation Board of Multi-turn LLM Agents
summary: Introduces AgentBoard, a multiturn agent evaluation framework with intermediate progress metrics and analysis tools. Its broader task suite includes WebShop and WebArena interactions with stepwise progress measurements.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract. The full paper documents search/click WebShop actions and 11 browser actions in WebArena, while the overall benchmark also covers non-web domains.

name: GPTVoiceTasker: Advancing Multi-step Mobile Task Efficiency Through Dynamic Interface Exploration and Learning
summary: Introduces GPTVoiceTasker, a mobile assistant that interprets user commands, executes device interactions, and learns from prior commands to streamline later task execution. The work includes a user study of task efficiency.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WIPI: A New Web Threat for LLM-Driven Web Agents
summary: Studies WIPI, a black-box indirect-instruction threat in which webpage content redirects LLM-driven web agents. Evaluation spans plugin-based agents, Web GPTs, and open-source web-agent implementations.

name: Enhancing Mobile "How-to" Queries with Automated Search Results Verification and Reranking

name: Grounded Language Agent for Product Search via Intelligent Web Interactions

name: Navigating WebAI: Training Agents to Complete Web Tasks with Large Language Models and Reinforcement Learning
summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement learning for MiniWoB web tasks and investigates whether agents understand HTML structure or memorize target elements.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Unveiling Disparities in Web Task Handling Between Human and Web Agent
summary: Compares human think-aloud web-task behavior with web-agent planning, action, and reflection. The analysis highlights differences in updating plans, handling ambiguity, and investigating failures.
notes: Reviewed against the retained original arXiv abstract.

name: V-Zen: Efficient GUI Understanding and Precise Grounding With A Novel Multimodal LLM
summary: Describes V-Zen, a multimodal GUI model with dual-resolution image encoders for grounding and next-action prediction, fine-tuned using GUIDE interface elements and task sequences.

name: WONDERBREAD: A Benchmark for Evaluating Multimodal Foundation Models on Business Process Management Tasks

summary: WebCoT turns reflection, look-ahead, branching and rollback procedures into chain-of-thought training rationales. Fine-tuning on these reconstructed trajectories is evaluated for web-agent self-improvement and transfer across navigation tasks.
name: WebCoT: Enhancing Web Agent Reasoning by Reconstructing Chain-of-Thought in Reflection, Branching, and Rollback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Uses an LLM judge to evaluate and filter synthetic GUI interaction trajectories for training a compact vision-language agent. OSWorld experiments assess the policy designed for local execution.
name: DPO Learning with LLMs-Judge Signal for Computer Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: AgentSynth composes easily generated subtasks into longer computer-use tasks and trajectories with adjustable difficulty. Its evaluation uses the number of subtasks to probe how agent success changes as task complexity grows.
name: AgentSynth: Scalable Task Generation for Generalist Computer-Use Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Introduces a finer-grained taxonomy of GUI localization errors and a logit-based Peak Sharpness Score for analyzing coordinate-prediction uncertainty. A context-aware cropping method refines the visual input without retraining the grounding model.
name: Understanding GUI Agent Localization Biases through Logit Sharpness
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Web-CogReasoner separates factual and conceptual web knowledge from procedural reasoning, using a structured curriculum to train a multimodal agent. Web-CogDataset and Web-CogBench support study of these capabilities alongside web-navigation evaluation.
name: Web-CogReasoner: Towards Multimodal Knowledge-Induced Cognitive Reasoning for Web Agents
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MVISU-Bench evaluates bilingual mobile tasks involving cross-app work, vague requests, user interaction and unethical instructions alongside ordinary single-app tasks. Its Aider prompting module is designed to clarify intent and mitigate risky execution within agent workflows.
name: MVISU-Bench: Benchmarking Mobile Agents for Real-World Tasks by Multi-App, Vague, Interactive, Single-App and Unethical Instructions
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: InquireMobile trains mobile agents to seek human confirmation at critical decisions using staged reinforcement fine-tuning and pre-action reasoning. InquireBench evaluates safe interaction and proactive inquiry, distinguishing asking for help from completing the underlying task.
name: InquireMobile: Teaching VLM-based Mobile Agent to Request Human Assistance via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GroundCUA turns expert desktop demonstrations into densely annotated screenshots and grounding instructions. The GroundNext model family uses this supervision and subsequent reinforcement learning, with both grounding benchmarks and an OSWorld agent configuration used for evaluation.
name: Grounding Computer Use Agents on Human Demonstrations
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MobileRAG combines retrieval and memory components to support mobile tasks that need external knowledge or long action sequences. MobileRAG-Eval is introduced to study these requirements on complex real-world app tasks.
name: MobileRAG: Enhancing Mobile Agent with Retrieval-Augmented Generation
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: BTL-UI separates GUI interaction into screen-region attention, planning and executable-command generation. It adds an automated annotation pipeline and rule-based process/outcome rewards for training, with evaluation on both static understanding and dynamic interaction.
name: BTL-UI: Blink-Think-Link Reasoning Model for GUI Agent
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-Cursor treats GUI grounding as a sequence of cursor movements guided by visible feedback and movement history. Online reinforcement learning with trajectory rewards trains the model to refine the target location across multiple steps.
name: Learning GUI Grounding with Spatial Reasoning from Visual Feedback
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: ProRe evaluates GUI task outcomes by having a reasoner assign targeted environment-probing tasks to specialist actors. The additional observations support reward judgments, with separate evaluation of judge accuracy and downstream agent task success.
name: ProRe: A Proactive Reward System for GUI Agents via Reasoner-Actor Collaboration
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-PRA evaluates GUI progress by generating task-specific criteria and actively inspecting visual evidence with tools. It tests offline judgment on OS-Critic Bench and the effects of this feedback on online mobile policies in AndroidWorld.
name: GUI-PRA: Process Reward Agent for GUI Tasks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WAREX augments existing web-agent benchmarks with reliability challenges arising from unstable systems and changing or disruptive website behavior. Evaluation on WebArena, WebVoyager and REAL examines how these disturbances affect task completion.
name: WAREX: Web Agent Reliability Evaluation on Existing Benchmarks
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GMS pairs a general vision-language scanner that proposes interface regions with a specialist locator that predicts coordinates within them. Hierarchical coarse-to-fine search coordinates the two components for GUI grounding on ScreenSpot-Pro.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: RAG-GUI trains a small guidance adapter to filter and summarize retrieved web tutorials while keeping the acting agent fixed. Supervised and rejection-sampling stages prepare the adapter for inference-time assistance, tested on offline web/mobile tasks and interactive Android tasks.
name: Retrieval-augmented GUI Agents with Generative Guidelines
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: PAL-UI combines observation/action summaries with selective retrieval of historical screenshots during planning. It trains mobile navigation models from step-level supervision and evaluates transfer to web navigation without additional training.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-KV compresses vision-language agents’ attention caches using visual-token saliency and redundancy between screenshot frames. The method requires no retraining and evaluates how cache budgets affect GUI action accuracy and computational cost.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WALT explores website functionality and converts demonstrated interactions into validated, reusable tools combining DOM actions, URL navigation, and agentic fallbacks. It evaluates this expanded browser action space on WebArena and VisualWebArena.

summary: BLIND-ACT tests whether computer-use agents persist with ambiguous, contradictory, or infeasible goals without adequate contextual reasoning. Its OSWorld-based tasks and judged trajectories examine these behaviors and the effect of mitigation prompts.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: This work addresses GUI localization errors caused by mismatches between visual patch positions and output pixel coordinates. RULER tokens provide explicit coordinate references, while Interleaved MRoPE balances width and height encoding; evaluation uses the ScreenSpot benchmark family.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: GUI-Spotlight trains a grounding model to reason over images and call tools that iteratively narrow its visual focus. The paper evaluates this refinement method on ScreenSpot-Pro after training on 18,500 samples.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: WARC-Bench packages dynamic web pages as replayable archives and evaluates short navigation subtasks involving components such as date pickers and scrollable containers. notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: R-WoM evaluates how well world models predict nearby GUI states, align complete procedures, and recognize milestone transitions. It retrieves external tutorials to guide simulated future interactions, with experiments on subsets of OSWorld and WebArena.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: ColorBench represents mobile tasks as graphs of states collected from real devices, providing a quasi-dynamic environment with multiple valid paths and error paths. It evaluates single-app and cross-app tasks using completion, subtask progress, and atomic diagnostics.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Surfer2 combines hierarchical context management with separate planning and execution, self-verification, and recovery for visual computer use. It evaluates the framework across web, desktop, and Android tasks without task-specific fine-tuning.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: OpenPhone trains a compact mobile policy with supervised learning followed by GRPO on synthetic GUI data, incorporating reasoning and memory management. Its device-cloud design handles routine work locally and delegates complex subtasks, with online evaluation on AndroidLab.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: HyperClick trains GUI grounders to produce a click and an accompanying confidence estimate using rewards for correctness and confidence alignment. Its evaluation examines localization, calibration, and abstention behavior.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: This work retrieves online video tutorials and converts them into structured GUI action demonstrations with short objectives. A two-stage selection process supplies a relevant local trajectory as in-context guidance at each execution step.

summary: HAR-GUI combines episodic reasoning and short-term memory to use earlier interactions when selecting GUI actions. Its training constructs reflective scenarios and correction guidance and applies a hybrid reinforcement-learning reward to the 3B policy.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: ProBench extends mobile GUI evaluation with tasks whose correctness depends on the interaction process as well as the final state. Its ProcessProvider supplies process information for assessing agent behavior and analyzing failure modes.

summary: Co-EPG alternates reinforcement learning for a planner with updates to a grounding model using generated training examples. The evolving grounder provides feedback to the planner, and evaluation uses Multimodal Mind2Web and AndroidControl.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: MVP addresses unstable GUI coordinates by predicting across several attention-guided cropped views. It clusters the resulting coordinates and selects the densest cluster centroid, evaluating this training-free inference method across grounding models.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained primary abstract.

summary: Step-GUI uses calibrated trajectory rewards to turn generated GUI interaction data into training signals for compact agent models. name: PLOW: A Collaborative Task Learning Agent
summary: Describes PLOW, which learns executable web-task models from a session combining demonstrations, natural-language explanations, and dialogue. Browser instrumentation connects user actions with DOM structure to support task generalization.

summary: Derives task graphs from demonstrated Android app interactions and layers a conversational question-answer interface over those graphs. The evaluation examines task-model extraction and developer use of the resulting bot templates.

name: Rousillon: Scraping Distributed Hierarchical Web Data
summary: Introduces Rousillon, which generalizes a demonstration of collecting one hierarchical data row into a browser-automation program that traverses related pages. The paper develops relation-selection and generalization methods and evaluates users building such scripts.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against retained primary publication sources. This is browser interaction learned from demonstrations, rather than a generic server-side crawling library.

summary: Introduces screenshot-based GUI search and visual scripting, using image patterns to locate interface targets and direct mouse and keyboard events. It evaluates screenshot queries and demonstrates automation and interactive-help tasks.
