name: Toward a Human-Centered Evaluation Framework for Trustworthy LLM-Powered GUI Agents
summary: Presents a position paper on privacy and security evaluation for GUI agents, identifying risk categories and challenges in involving human evaluators. It proposes risk-aware assessment and in-context consent as design directions.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a position paper proposing an evaluation framework; the abstract does not report a new benchmark or empirical validation of the proposed framework.

name: OSUniverse: Benchmark for Multimodal GUI-navigation AI Agents
summary: Introduces OSUniverse, a desktop GUI benchmark spanning precise clicks through multistep and multiapplication tasks. It provides both manual scoring and an automated validation mechanism.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: Do MLLMs Capture How Interfaces Guide User Behavior? A Benchmark for Multimodal UI/UX Design Understanding
summary: Introduces WiserUI-Bench, pairing real UI variants from industry A/B tests with observed behavioral winners and expert explanations. It evaluates models’ ability to predict the more effective interface and explain its effect on user behavior.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available. This benchmark measures UI/UX design understanding from static image pairs; it does not measure autonomous GUI action execution.

name: Characterizing Unintended Consequences in Human-GUI Agent Collaboration for Web Browsing
summary: Studies unintended consequences of collaborative web browsing with GUI agents through social-media analysis and interviews. It organizes observed failures, user impacts, and mitigation practices around planning, interface interaction, feedback, privacy, and trust.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Creating General User Models from Computer Use
summary: Proposes general user models that turn computer-use observations into confidence-weighted propositions and revise them as new context arrives. Demonstrations use this memory to contextualize assistants, manage notifications, and support proactive actions across apps.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: EVA: Evolving Semantic Adversaries for Red-Teaming GUI Agents Against Environmental Injection Attacks
summary: Introduces EVA, a red-teaming framework that evolves semantic payloads for GUI environmental-injection tests. It studies the contribution of semantic versus visual deception and distills discovered patterns into reusable evaluation rules.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Hidden Ghost Hand: Unveiling Backdoor Vulnerabilities in MLLM-Powered Mobile GUI Agents
summary: Studies backdoor risks in mobile GUI agents through AgentGhost, which combines goal-level and interaction-history triggers during model training. The paper evaluates multiple mobile agents and a tailored defense.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ScreenExplorer: Training a Vision-Language Model for Diverse Exploration in Open GUI World
summary: Trains ScreenExplorer with reinforcement learning in dynamic GUI environments, using a world-model curiosity reward and experience-stream distillation to support sustained exploration.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: AdInject: Real-World Black-Box Attacks on Web Agents via Advertising Delivery
summary: Studies advertising delivery as an indirect-injection channel for web agents under a black-box threat model. AdInject evaluates how static ad content shaped by website context can redirect browser actions.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: UI-Evol: Automatic Knowledge Evolving for Computer Use Agents
summary: Introduces UI-Evol, which extracts action sequences from agent interactions and critiques external guidance against those traces. Evaluation on OSWorld examines how revised operational knowledge affects execution and behavioral consistency.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: RiOSWorld: Benchmarking the Risk of Multimodal Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces RiOSWorld, a computer-use risk benchmark separating user-originated and environmental threats. It evaluates both risky-goal intent and goal completion across web and other computer applications.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VPI-Bench: Visual Prompt Injection Attacks for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces VPI-Bench, interactive web-platform variants containing visually embedded malicious instructions. It evaluates computer-use and browser-use agents under these threats and examines system-prompt defenses.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: VerificAgent: Domain-Specific Memory Verification for Scalable Oversight of Aligned Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces VerificAgent, which grows domain-specific memories from task trajectories and subjects them to human fact-checking before deployment. Its OSWorld evaluation treats persistent memory as an auditable constraint on later agent behavior.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUIPilot: A Consistency-based Mobile GUI Testing Approach for Detecting Application-specific Bugs
summary: Introduces GUIPilot, which compares mobile design mock-ups with implemented screens through widget alignment and tests expected transitions by executing inferred UI actions. It evaluates both visual inconsistencies and workflow-specific bugs.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: EconWebArena: Benchmarking Autonomous Agents on Economic Tasks in Realistic Web Environments
summary: Introduces EconWebArena, a curated benchmark of economic-data tasks requiring live website navigation, multimodal interpretation, and precise extraction. It evaluates visual grounding, planning, and interaction design within multistep workflows.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: UITron-Speech: Towards Automated GUI Agents Based on Speech Instructions
summary: Introduces UITron-Speech, which predicts GUI actions from spoken instructions and screenshots. It combines synthetic speech data and mixed-modality training with a training-free grounding refinement step.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Context manipulation attacks : Web agents are susceptible to corrupted memory
summary: Studies context manipulation in web agents by altering stored task representations rather than webpage prompts alone. Evaluation on Browser-use and Agent-E examines memory-directed attacks and the implications for secure context handling.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Mobile GUI Agents under Real-world Threats: Are We There Yet?
summary: Introduces an app-content instrumentation framework and complementary interactive and static test suites for mobile GUI agents. It studies how untrusted third-party content changes task execution and state understanding.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: A Systematization of Security Vulnerabilities in Computer Use Agents
summary: Analyzes security boundaries in computer-use agents through a risk taxonomy and concrete adversarial case studies. It links observed failures to input provenance, interface-action binding, memory, and delegation, and proposes CUA-specific evaluation principles.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. This is a threat analysis with case studies; the annotation does not imply a standardized public benchmark or independently validated defenses.

name: VisualTrap: A Stealthy Backdoor Attack on GUI Agents via Visual Grounding Manipulation
summary: Studies backdoors that redirect GUI visual grounding even when the task plan is correct. VisualTrap evaluates whether poisoned grounding training transfers to downstream tasks and across web, mobile, and desktop interface settings.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: LaSM: Layer-wise Scaling Mechanism for Defending Pop-up Attack on GUI Agents
summary: Introduces LaSM, a training-free defense that selectively scales attention and MLP components to improve alignment with task-relevant screen regions. It evaluates the approach against pop-up-based GUI injection attacks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebGuard: Building a Generalizable Guardrail for Web Agents
summary: Introduces WebGuard, a human-annotated dataset for predicting outcomes and risk levels of state-changing website actions. It provides generalization splits and evaluates specialized guardrail models.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Manipulating LLM Web Agents with Indirect Prompt Injection Attack via HTML Accessibility Tree
summary: Studies indirect prompt injection through HTML content consumed as accessibility trees. The evaluation tests how manipulated page observations redirect browser-agent actions on real websites.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GuirlVG: Incentivize GUI Visual Grounding via Empirical Exploration on Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces GuirlVG, an empirical study of reinforcement fine-tuning for GUI visual grounding. It analyzes training components and adds an adaptive KL-based mechanism to limit reward over-optimization.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: Morae: Proactively Pausing UI Agents for User Choices
summary: Introduces Morae, a UI agent that detects decision points and pauses for user choices using interface code and screenshots. A study with blind and low-vision participants evaluates this mixed-initiative approach on real web tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: MobiAgent: A Systematic Framework for Customizable Mobile Agents
summary: Presents MobiAgent, combining MobiMind agent models, the AgentRR acceleration framework, and MobiFlow evaluation. It also introduces an AI-assisted data-collection pipeline for mobile GUI tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: SparkUI-Parser: Enhancing GUI Perception with Robust Grounding and Parsing
summary: Introduces SparkUI-Parser, which adds continuous coordinate decoding and a rejection mechanism for nonexistent targets to a multimodal model. It also presents ScreenParse for evaluating structural interface perception.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: VeriOS: Query-Driven Proactive Human-Agent-GUI Interaction for Trustworthy OS Agents
summary: Introduces VeriOS-Agent, which learns when to execute GUI actions autonomously and when to query a user under untrustworthy conditions. Its staged training combines supervised learning and group-relative policy optimization.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: AgentSentinel: An End-to-End and Real-Time Security Defense Framework for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces AgentSentinel, which intercepts sensitive computer-agent operations and audits them using task context together with system traces. BadComputerUse evaluates this enforcement approach across attack scenarios involving tool and computer control.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The official full paper confirms GUI/desktop interaction alongside Bash and file tools. Its abstract and body enumerate attack categories differently; no category count is promoted into this annotation.

name: Dark Patterns Meet GUI Agents: LLM Agent Susceptibility to Manipulative Interfaces and the Role of Human Oversight
summary: Studies how GUI agents, people, and human-agent teams respond to manipulative interface designs. The two-phase evaluation examines failure modes and the benefits and costs of human oversight.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Environmental Injection Attacks against GUI Agents in Realistic Dynamic Environments
summary: Introduces Chameleon, an environmental-injection evaluation framework that varies webpage content and trigger context. It combines simulated page variation with attention-based optimization and tests GUI agents across realistic websites.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: PrivWeb: Unobtrusive and Content-aware Privacy Protection For Web Agents
summary: Introduces PrivWeb, which uses a local language model to anonymize interface information according to user preferences. Adaptive notifications and selective pauses give users control over sensitive information access during web-agent tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: See, Think, Act: Teaching Multimodal Agents to Effectively Interact with GUI by Identifying Toggles
summary: Introduces a benchmark for binary GUI-toggle instructions and State-aware Reasoning, which compares the observed control state with the requested state before choosing an action. It evaluates agents on toggle tasks and broader interactive benchmarks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available.

name: OS-Sentinel: Towards Safety-Enhanced Mobile GUI Agents via Hybrid Validation in Realistic Workflows
summary: Introduces MobileRisk-Live and OS-Sentinel, combining a formal verifier for system-level violations with a multimodal judge for contextual risks in mobile GUI workflows.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Auto-scaling Continuous Memory for GUI Agent
summary: Encodes GUI trajectories into compact continuous embeddings that can be retrieved directly into an agent’s input. An automated environment-discovery and rollout pipeline expands this memory for long tasks and unfamiliar interfaces.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Hi-Agent: Hierarchical Vision-Language Agents for Mobile Device Control
summary: Introduces Hi-Agent, jointly training a high-level reasoning model and a low-level mobile action model. Execution feedback supplies a foresight advantage for optimizing subgoal decisions, with evaluations on Android control benchmarks.
notes: Reviewed against the exact-version official arXiv abstract page; its complete title, ordered author list, visible version, and normalized abstract SHA match the retained snapshot. The original API response body was not locally available. This Hi-Agent has a distinct author team and method from the earlier HiAgent working-memory paper; the shared project-name prefix is not treated as an identity match.

name: ReInAgent: A Context-Aware GUI Agent Enabling Human-in-the-Loop Mobile Task Navigation
summary: Introduces ReInAgent, coordinating information management, planning, and reflection around a shared memory for mobile tasks. It proactively asks users for information and checks consistency when instructions are ambiguous or change during execution.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OpenApps: Simulating Environment Variations to Measure UI-Agent Reliability
summary: Introduces OpenApps, a configurable app ecosystem for measuring UI-agent reliability under changes in appearance and content. Its evaluation compares task success and failure behavior across many versions of the same apps.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUI Exploration Lab: Enhancing Screen Navigation in Agents via Multi-Turn Reinforcement Learning
summary: Introduces GUI Exploration Lab, a simulation engine for composing screens, interface elements, and navigation graphs. It studies how supervised learning, single-turn RL, and multiturn RL affect GUI navigation and exploration.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AgentProg: Empowering Long-Horizon GUI Agents with Program-Guided Context Management
summary: Introduces AgentProg, organizing mobile-agent interaction history as a program with variables and control flow to decide what context to retain. A global belief state handles partial observability, with evaluation on AndroidWorld and extended long-horizon tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebGym: Scaling Training Environments for Visual Web Agents with Realistic Tasks
summary: WebGym supplies realistic web tasks with rubric-based evaluation and an asynchronous rollout system for reinforcement learning. It studies how training on an agent’s own interaction traces scales with task coverage and transfers to unseen websites.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MobileDreamer: Generative Sketch World Model for GUI Agent
summary: MobileDreamer predicts post-action GUI states as task-relevant textual sketches with an order-invariant learning objective. Agents use these predictions for lookahead action selection, evaluated on AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: InfiniteWeb: Scalable Web Environment Synthesis for GUI Agent Training
summary: InfiniteWeb generates functional, interconnected websites and task evaluators using shared specifications and task-driven development. It evaluates website construction and the transfer of GUI policies trained in these synthetic web environments to OSWorld and Online-Mind2Web.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: From Off-Policy to On-Policy: Enhancing GUI Agents via Bi-level Expert-to-Policy Assimilation
summary: BEPA adapts a small set of expert GUI traces into policy-aligned guidance through trajectories reachable by the learner and a dynamically updated task cache. It evaluates this two-level approach to reinforcement learning on desktop and web benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ColorBrowserAgent: Complex Long-Horizon Browser Agent with Adaptive Knowledge Evolution
summary: ColorBrowserAgent converts human feedback into reusable website knowledge and uses that knowledge to guide progressive context summaries. It evaluates the resulting memory and adaptation mechanisms on long browser workflows.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: OS-Symphony: A Holistic Framework for Robust and Generalist Computer-Using Agent
summary: OS-Symphony coordinates milestone-based reflection and memory with tools that build visually aligned tutorials through browser interaction. The framework evaluates trajectory correction and adaptation on online computer-use benchmarks including OSWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ExpSeek: Self-Triggered Experience Seeking for Web Agents
summary: ExpSeek uses step-level entropy signals to decide when a web agent should request experience-based guidance. It supplies guidance tailored to the current step and evaluates the intervention across web-agent benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GUI-Eyes: Tool-Augmented Perception for Visual Grounding in GUI Agents
summary: GUI-Eyes trains GUI grounders to decide when and how to use visual tools such as crops and zooms. Its coarse-to-fine policy uses dense spatial rewards based on location proximity and region overlap, with evaluation on ScreenSpot-Pro.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: System-level Security for Computer Use Agents
summary: NOVA separates trusted task planning from screen-derived observations by producing a branching plan before execution and resolving runtime values through perception. Its OSWorld study examines security and utility while identifying remaining risks from perception-driven branch steering.
verify_terms: CaMeLs Can Use Computers Too: Sy
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Compress to Focus: Efficient Coordinate Compression for Policy Optimization in Multi-Turn GUI Agents
summary: CCPO couples GUI policy optimization with coordinate-guided compression of past visual observations. It aggregates targets across rollouts to focus retained context and uses distance-based advantages to train grounding and compression together.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MirrorGuard: Toward Secure Computer-Use Agents via Simulation-to-Real Reasoning Correction
summary: MirrorGuard trains a reasoning-correction defense using GUI risk trajectories generated in a text-based neural-symbolic simulator. It evaluates whether corrections transfer to computer-use agents operating real interfaces, keeping simulated training separate from deployment tests.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MagicGUI-RMS: A Multi-Agent Reward Model System for Self-Evolving GUI Agents via Automated Feedback Reflux
summary: MagicGUI-RMS combines domain-specific and general reward models to assess GUI actions and propose corrections. A structured data pipeline and feedback-recycling process support repeated reward-model and agent improvement.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: EvoCUA: Evolving Computer Use Agents via Learning from Scalable Synthetic Experience
summary: EvoCUA combines task synthesis with executable validators, asynchronous sandbox rollouts and iterative policy updates. It turns successful routines and analyzed failures into supervision and evaluates the evolving agent on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GraphPilot: GUI Task Automation with One-Step LLM Reasoning Powered by Knowledge Graph
summary: GraphPilot builds app-specific knowledge graphs from explored pages, elements and transitions, then uses them to plan action sequences. It requests additional interface observations when uncertain and checks plans against graph transition rules before correction and execution.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GAIA: A Data Flywheel System for Training GUI Test-Time Scaling Critic Models
summary: GAIA trains a GUI action critic on positive and negative examples, then uses that critic to collect improved examples for another training round. It studies how recycling these data affects the test-time action choices of different GUI agents.

notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MAGNET: Towards Adaptive GUI Agents with Memory-Driven Knowledge Evolution
summary: MAGNET maintains separate memories for stable interface functions and task procedures across changing layouts and workflows. It updates frequently used knowledge and evaluates adaptation in AndroidWorld and offline distribution-shift settings.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: OmegaUse: Building a General-Purpose GUI Agent for Autonomous Task Execution
summary: OmegaUse combines exploratory and taxonomy-guided data synthesis with supervised fine-tuning followed by GRPO for GUI control. The report introduces OS-Nav for offline Android and Ubuntu evaluation alongside established grounding and action-prediction benchmarks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Continual GUI Agents
summary: Continual GUI Agents defines grounding under changing application domains and screen resolutions. Its GUI-AiF training framework uses separate point- and region-alignment rewards to adapt grounding as these distributions shift.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: CUA-Skill: Develop Skills for Computer Using Agent
summary: CUA-Skill encodes Windows application knowledge in parameterized skills and execution/composition graphs. Its agent retrieves and instantiates these skills and uses memory for failure recovery, with end-to-end evaluation on WindowsAgentArena.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: BEAP-Agent: Backtrackable Execution and Adaptive Planning for GUI Agents
summary: BEAP-Agent treats GUI execution as depth-first search with coordinated planning, execution and task-state tracking. It supports backtracking across multiple levels of earlier states and evaluates recovery on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: WebArbiter: A Principle-Guided Reasoning Process Reward Model for Web Agents
summary: WebArbiter generates reasoned action-preference verdicts for web navigation, using reasoning distillation followed by reinforcement learning. It introduces WebPRMBench and evaluates both preference judgments and reward-guided trajectory search.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: DynaWeb: Model-Based Reinforcement Learning of Web Agents
summary: DynaWeb learns a world model that predicts web-page representations after actions and uses it to generate policy-training rollouts. It interleaves these rollouts with expert trajectories and evaluates the trained web agents on WebArena and WebVoyager.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Darwinian Memory: A Training-Free Self-Regulating Memory System for GUI Agent Evolution
summary: Darwinian Memory splits GUI trajectories into reusable units and updates the memory by retaining useful paths and pruning poor ones. It evaluates this training-free memory mechanism on long multi-application tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Learning with Challenges: Adaptive Difficulty-Aware Data Generation for Mobile GUI Agent Training
summary: MobileGen estimates a mobile agent’s strengths across structural and semantic task difficulty, then samples new training targets around that profile. A controllable multi-agent generator creates the corresponding instructions and GUI trajectories.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Agentic Reward Modeling: Verifying GUI Agent via Progressive Trajectory-Grounded Interaction
summary: VAGEN verifies GUI trajectories by first extracting readily available evidence and escalating to tool-based environment probes when needed. Evaluation on OSWorld-Verified and AndroidWorld studies verification accuracy and its cost.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Generative Visual Code Mobile World Models
summary: gWorld predicts future mobile GUI states as renderable web code and supplies an automated pipeline for code-based training data. The study evaluates visual state prediction and how stronger world models affect downstream mobile policies.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: SafePred: A Predictive Guardrail for Computer-Using Agents via World Models
summary: SafePred uses world-model risk forecasts to guide action filtering and task replanning. Its desktop and web safety evaluations distinguish policy compliance, task success and success under the specified policy.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.

name: Avenir-Web: Human-Experience-Imitating Multimodal Web Agents with Mixture of Grounding Experts
summary: Avenir-Web combines multiple grounding specialists with procedural experience, a task checklist and adaptive memory. It evaluates this planning and execution framework on live Online-Mind2Web tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ToolTok: Tool Tokenization for Efficient and Generalizable GUI Agents
summary: ToolTok represents GUI operations with learned tool tokens and frames interaction as progressive tool selection. Semantic anchoring and an easy-to-hard curriculum teach tool meanings before visual pathfinding, with evaluation across grounding scenarios.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Agent Alpha: Tree Search Unifying Generation, Exploration and Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Agent Alpha uses step-level Monte Carlo tree search to reuse successful prefixes and recover from early GUI mistakes. Comparison-based evaluation and diversity-constrained expansion guide the search, with experiments on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: WebSentinel: Detecting and Localizing Prompt Injection Attacks for Web Agents
summary: WebSentinel identifies suspicious webpage segments and checks each against its surrounding page context to detect and locate prompt injections. Its evaluation uses both contaminated and clean webpage datasets.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: M$^2$-Miner: Multi-Agent Enhanced MCTS for Mobile GUI Agent Data Mining
summary: M2-Miner uses multi-agent-guided Monte Carlo tree search to collect mobile GUI intent–trajectory pairs. Intent recycling and progressive collector training aim to increase the diversity and usefulness of the mined interaction data.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: UI-Mem: Self-Evolving Experience Memory for Online Reinforcement Learning in Mobile GUI Agents
summary: UI-Mem stores workflows, skills and failure patterns as reusable templates to guide online GUI reinforcement learning. It varies guidance within rollout groups and continually updates the memory so an unguided policy can learn from guided experiences.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
summary: MemGUI-Bench evaluates short-term retention and cross-session experience reuse in mobile GUI agents using paired tasks and repeated-attempt protocols. Its staged evaluator measures memory fidelity, learning and execution efficiency.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Trifuse: Enhancing Attention-Based GUI Grounding via Multimodal Fusion
summary: Trifuse combines attention-based localization with OCR text cues and icon captions to ground GUI instructions. Its fusion procedure favors cross-modal agreement and sharp location peaks, and is evaluated without task-specific fine-tuning.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ANCHOR: Branch-Point Data Generation for GUI Agents
summary: ANCHOR expands verified desktop demonstrations by generating new tasks at meaningful branch points and executing their instructions. State-aware verification and action filtering refine the resulting trajectories, which are evaluated through fine-tuned agents on OSWorld and WindowsAgentArena.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: When Actions Go Off-Task: Detecting and Correcting Misaligned Actions in Computer-Use Agents
summary: MisActBench provides action-level labels for task alignment, while DeAction checks proposed computer-use actions and requests revisions through structured feedback. The paper separately evaluates offline detection and interactive operation in OSWorld and RedTeamCUA.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.

name: TreeCUA: Efficiently Scaling GUI Automation with Tree-Structured Verifiable Evolution
summary: TreeCUA organizes GUI exploration trajectories as reusable trees and balances deeper tasks against broader coverage. Its data pipeline combines action verification, memory-backed recovery and a DPO variant that uses information from adjacent branches.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Code2World: A GUI World Model via Renderable Code Generation
summary: Code2World predicts future GUI screens through renderable code, trained on AndroidCode trajectories with supervised learning and render-aware reinforcement learning. It evaluates visual prediction and downstream AndroidWorld navigation with the learned world model.
verify_terms: Code2World: A GUI World Model vi
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Autonomous Continual Learning for Environment Adaptation of Computer-Use Agents
summary: ACuRL uses autonomous interface exploration and an adaptive task curriculum to continually train computer-use policies with reinforcement learning. CUAJudge supplies outcome feedback, and experiments study adaptation across desktop applications and environment changes.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract and the specified sections of the same recorded paper version.

name: Adaptive Milestone Reward for GUI Agents
summary: ADMIRE extracts milestones from successful GUI explorations to provide adaptive intermediate rewards. It assigns credit differently to successful and failed trajectories and evaluates training on AndroidWorld, with additional transfer studies in web and embodied settings.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Agentic Test-Time Scaling for WebAgents
summary: CATTS allocates additional inference computation when an agent’s action votes show uncertainty. The paper compares voting and arbiter strategies and evaluates this selective scaling on WebArena-Lite, Online-Mind2Web and GoBrowse.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Scaling Web Agent Training through Automatic Data Generation and Fine-grained Evaluation
summary: This work uses constraint-based progress evaluation to retain partially successful web trajectories for training. It introduces BookingArena for structured booking tasks and studies a distilled agent trained with the resulting data.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Building Autonomous GUI Navigation via Agentic-Q Estimation and Step-Wise Policy Optimization
summary: This framework learns an agentic-Q model to estimate individual actions’ contributions to GUI task completion. It then optimizes a policy with step-level samples from its own trajectories, decoupling policy updates from environment interaction.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: GUI-GENESIS: Automated Synthesis of Efficient Environments with Verifiable Rewards for GUI Agent Post-Training
summary: GUI-GENESIS reconstructs applications as lightweight web environments with executable assertions for reward computation. It evaluates the cost of these training environments and transfer from synthetic interaction training to held-out real tasks.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ScreenParse: Moving Beyond Sparse Grounding with Complete Screen Parsing Supervision
summary: ScreenParse supplies dense annotations of UI elements, types and text in web screenshots through an automated rendering and filtering pipeline. ScreenVLM learns to output structured screen markup, and the study evaluates dense parsing and transfer to GUI grounding.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AutoWebWorld: Synthesizing Infinite Verifiable Web Environments via Finite State Machines
summary: AutoWebWorld turns finite-state task models into interactive websites whose actions and goal states can be checked programmatically. It generates verified trajectories for training and evaluates transfer to WebVoyager and Online-Mind2Web.
notes: The annotation was reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Sikuli legacy research implementation

MIT applies to project code; external libraries keep their own terms.

name: WebWorld: A Large-Scale World Model for Web Agent Training

name: Computer-Using World Model

notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: CGL: Advancing Continual GUI Learning via Reinforcement Fine-Tuning
summary: Combines supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning for continual GUI learning, using policy entropy to adjust their proportions and gradient projection to limit conflicting updates. AndroidControl-CL groups applications into sequential tasks to evaluate adaptation and retention.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract describes artifact release as future work; this annotation does not assert current availability.

name: Dual-Modality Multi-Stage Adversarial Safety Training: Robustifying Multimodal Web Agents Against Cross-Modal Attacks
summary: Studies webpage injections that affect both screenshots and accessibility trees, then trains web agents through teacher imitation, supervised adversarial examples, and adversarial reinforcement learning. The evaluation tests defenses on MiniWoB++ and held-out tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebFactory: Automated Compression of Foundational Language Intelligence into Grounded Web Agents
summary: Introduces WebFactory, a GUI-agent training pipeline that synthesizes websites, generates tasks and trajectories, and trains with decomposed rewards. Offline and online transfer evaluations examine agents trained on the generated environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Generalization in Online Reinforcement Learning for Mobile Agents
summary: Introduces AndroidWorld-Generalization with separate tests for unseen task instances, templates, and applications. A GRPO training system combines containerized environments with asynchronous trajectory collection to study these generalization regimes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OSExpert: Computer-Use Agents Learning Professional Skills via Exploration
summary: Uses GUI-based depth-first exploration to verify elementary software functions, assemble action primitives, and construct curricula of composed skills. OSExpert-Eval examines how the resulting procedural knowledge supports complex computer-use tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: SecAgent: Efficient Mobile GUI Agent with Semantic Context
summary: Presents a Chinese mobile GUI dataset and navigation benchmark together with SecAgent, which compresses previous screenshots and actions into semantic summaries. The agent is trained with supervised and reinforcement fine-tuning to use this compact interaction context.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Mobile use is explicit, but the abstract does not identify a mobile operating system.

name: Video-Based Reward Modeling for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Builds ExeVR-53k from execution-video, instruction and reward triplets, including negative instructions with step annotations. A reward model uses spatiotemporal token pruning to judge task completion from the instruction and execution keyframes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Safe and Scalable Web Agent Learning via Recreated Websites
summary: Introduces VeriEnv, which recreates websites as executable training environments and exposes internal state through a Python SDK for task generation and deterministic reward checks. Experiments examine web-agent learning across new and expanded site environments.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract promises a release upon acceptance; this annotation does not verify artifact availability.

name: HATS: Hardness-Aware Trajectory Synthesis for GUI Agents
summary: Introduces HATS, which directs GUI trajectory exploration toward semantically ambiguous actions and iteratively checks instruction-execution alignment. Feedback from trajectory refinement updates the exploration signal used to collect subsequent training examples.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Zoom to Essence: Trainless GUI Grounding by Inferring upon Interface Elements
summary: Presents ZoomUI, a training-free grounding method that expresses instructions as visual element descriptions and uses model attention to zoom progressively into relevant interface regions. Evaluation examines instruction-to-element localization on GUI benchmarks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents
summary: Formalizes a visual confused-deputy failure in which a computer agent acts on a misperceived UI object. A separate guardrail checks both the visual target and the agent's action reasoning against deployment-specific knowledge before permitting execution.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AdaZoom-GUI: Adaptive Zoom-based GUI Grounding with Instruction Refinement
summary: Combines instruction rewriting with conditional second-stage zooming for small GUI targets. A grounding dataset and GRPO training support joint prediction of click coordinates and element bounding boxes.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AndroTMem: From Interaction Trajectories to Anchored Memory in Long-Horizon GUI Agents
summary: Introduces AndroTMem-Bench for Android tasks whose later actions depend on earlier UI states. Anchored State Memory retains causally linked intermediate states for subgoal-specific retrieval and evaluates them against full-history and summary-based memory.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OS-Themis: A Scalable Critic Framework for Generalist GUI Rewards
summary: Presents OS-Themis, a multi-agent critic that divides GUI trajectories into verifiable milestones and reviews their evidence before assigning an outcome. OGRBench evaluates GUI rewards across platforms, with AndroidWorld experiments examining training and trajectory filtering.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ContractSkill: Repairable Contract-Based Skills for Multimodal Web Agents
summary: Turns draft web-agent skills into structured executable artifacts that support deterministic checks, fault localization and local repair. VisualWebArena and MiniWoB experiments examine execution and reuse within the same benchmark family.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract limits its portability evidence to transfer within a benchmark family, not generalization across arbitrary benchmarks.

name: UI-Voyager: A Self-Evolving GUI Agent Learning via Failed Experience
summary: Introduces a two-stage mobile GUI learner that first co-evolves trajectories and policies through rejection fine-tuning. Group Relative Self-Distillation then uses successful rollout branches to provide step-level supervision for failed trajectories, evaluated on AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebTestBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents towards End-to-End Automated Web Testing
summary: Introduces WebTestBench for end-to-end website testing, separating checklist generation from defect detection. Its WebTester baseline evaluates test coverage, detection and sustained interaction across web application categories.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Where and How to Prune: An Empirical Study of Visual Token Pruning for GUI Agent Navigation
summary: Studies visual token pruning for GUI navigation, separating reusable screenshot encoder embeddings from later language-model computation. The analysis examines foreground-background token allocation and spatial coverage when pruning historical screenshots.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Towards GUI Agents: Vision-Language Diffusion Models for GUI Grounding
summary: Adapts a discrete vision-language diffusion model to single-turn GUI action and bounding-box prediction, using a hybrid masking schedule for coordinate geometry. Experiments across web, desktop and mobile datasets examine grounding accuracy and inference tradeoffs.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Emergence WebVoyager: Toward Consistent and Transparent Evaluation of (Web) Agents in The Wild
summary: Audits sources of ambiguity and operational variation in WebVoyager evaluation and introduces standardized guidance for task setup, failure handling, annotation and reporting. Emergence WebVoyager applies this protocol to a web-agent evaluation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GPA: Learning GUI Process Automation from Demonstrations
summary: Presents demonstration-based GUI process replay with Sequential Monte Carlo localization and readiness checks. GPA executes the learned workflow locally and can serve as the GUI execution component of an agent using MCP or CLI tools.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Poison Once, Exploit Forever: Environment-Injected Memory Poisoning Attacks on Web Agents
summary: Studies persistent web-agent memory contamination introduced through environmental observations instead of direct memory access. Experiments on WebArena and VisualWebArena examine cross-session effects and how interaction failures alter susceptibility.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Comparing Human Oversight Strategies for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Compares four human oversight strategies during live web-agent sessions, examining exposure to problematic actions and opportunities to intervene. The analysis identifies timing and attention problems in control handoffs and upfront plan approval.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: IntentScore: Intent-Conditioned Action Evaluation for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Trains IntentScore on offline desktop GUI interactions to assess candidate actions using both their state relevance and planning intent. The reward model is evaluated as an action reranker for Agent S3 on OSWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Don't Act Blindly: Robust GUI Automation via Action-Effect Verification and Self-Correction
summary: Introduces VeriGUI, which checks expected action effects and reasons about recovery before subsequent GUI actions. Training combines synthetic failure trajectories with verification-weighted GRPO, evaluated on an AndroidControl-based robustness benchmark.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Gym-Anything: Turn any Software into an Agent Environment
summary: Introduces Gym-Anything, where a setup agent configures software environments and an independent auditor checks the resulting evidence. CUA-World supplies long-horizon tasks across professional applications, with experiments on trajectory distillation and test-time auditing.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: The Art of Building Verifiers for Computer Use Agents
summary: Describes a web-trajectory verifier built around structured rubrics, separate process and outcome judgments, and explicit treatment of uncontrollable failures. CUAVerifierBench supplies human labels for evaluating these choices and screenshot-based context management.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: What's Missing in Screen-to-Action? Towards a UI-in-the-Loop Paradigm for Multimodal GUI Reasoning
summary: Introduces UILoop, which inserts explicit UI-element localization, function and usage reasoning between screen observation and action. UI Comprehension-Bench evaluates these element-level capabilities with three metrics.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Android Coach: Improve Online Agentic Training Efficiency with Single State Multiple Actions
summary: Introduces Android Coach, which uses a learned critic to evaluate multiple candidate actions at each observed emulator state. Process rewards and a group-wise advantage estimator support online training, evaluated on AndroidLab and AndroidWorld.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: MolmoWeb: Open Visual Web Agent and Open Data for the Open Web
summary: Presents MolmoWebMix, combining synthetic browser trajectories, human demonstrations and GUI perception data, and MolmoWeb screenshot-to-action policies trained from it. Browser benchmarks also test parallel rollouts with best-of-N selection.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract states that artifacts will be released; this annotation does not independently verify release status or licenses.

name: CORA: Conformal Risk-Controlled Agents for Safeguarded Mobile GUI Automation
summary: Introduces CORA, which calibrates a risk model to choose between executing and abstaining from mobile GUI actions, then diagnoses rejected actions to suggest interventions. Phone-Harm provides step-level safety labels for evaluating this safeguarding process.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The annotation describes risk calibration without asserting an unconditional safety guarantee.

name: HealthAdminBench: Evaluating Computer-Use Agents on Healthcare Administration Tasks
summary: Introduces HealthAdminBench with GUI environments for an electronic health record, payer portals and fax handling. Expert-defined administrative tasks are decomposed into verifiable subtasks to compare local progress with end-to-end workflow completion.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WebForge: Breaking the Realism-Reproducibility-Scalability Trilemma in Browser Agent Benchmark
summary: Presents WebForge, a pipeline that plans, generates, refines and validates self-contained interactive websites. WebForge-Bench uses these environments to evaluate browser agents across domains and controlled difficulty levels.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ClawGUI: A Unified Framework for Training, Evaluating, and Deploying GUI Agents
summary: Presents ClawGUI, a shared harness for GUI-agent reinforcement learning, benchmark evaluation and deployment on mobile devices. It combines parallel virtual and physical environments, process rewards, and hybrid CLI-GUI execution with persistent memory.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: PrecisionCUA: Iterative Visual Refinement for Pixel-Precise Cursor Grounding in Code Editors
summary: Studies iterative cursor grounding in dense code-editor interfaces, using visual feedback from earlier attempts to correct displacement. PrecisionCUA evaluates this closed-loop process across multiple model families on coding-interface tasks.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: UI-Zoomer: Uncertainty-Driven Adaptive Zoom-In for GUI Grounding
summary: Introduces UI-Zoomer, a training-free grounding method that uses candidate agreement and token confidence to decide when to crop and retry. Prediction variance determines a separate crop radius for each uncertain interface target.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: GUI-Perturbed: Domain Randomization Reveals Systematic Brittleness in GUI Grounding Models
summary: Introduces GUI-Perturbed, which varies screenshot appearance and instruction wording independently to diagnose grounding failures. Experiments on three related model architectures examine relational instructions, browser zoom and augmentation-based fine-tuning.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: FedGUI: Benchmarking Federated GUI Agents across Heterogeneous Platforms, Devices, and Operating Systems
summary: Introduces FedGUI, a federated GUI-learning benchmark built from six datasets spanning mobile, web and desktop interfaces. Its experiments separate platform, device, operating-system and data-source heterogeneity when evaluating collaborative training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OpenMobile: Building Open Mobile Agents with Task and Trajectory Synthesis
summary: Presents OpenMobile, which builds exploration-based environment memory to synthesize task instructions and switches between learner and expert policies during trajectory collection. The resulting data includes recovery behavior and is tested through mobile-agent training and benchmark-overlap analysis.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: HalluClear: Diagnosing, Evaluating and Mitigating Hallucinations in GUI Agents
summary: Introduces HalluClear with a GUI hallucination taxonomy, expert-calibrated evaluation workflow and structured-reasoning post-training scheme. It evaluates how these components affect hallucinations, grounding and action fidelity across GUI agents.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Measure Twice, Click Once: Co-evolving Proposer and Visual Critic via Reinforcement Learning for GUI Grounding
summary: Trains a GUI grounding proposer together with a visual critic that evaluates candidate locations rendered on screenshots. An adaptive reinforcement-learning schedule balances their development, using proposal diversity and critic feedback during training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Odysseys: Benchmarking Web Agents on Realistic Long Horizon Tasks
summary: Introduces Odysseys, a live-web benchmark of long, multi-site tasks derived from browsing sessions. Graded task rubrics and a rubric-score-per-step measure evaluate both partial progress and trajectory efficiency.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Benchmarking and Improving GUI Agents in High-Dynamic Environments
summary: Introduces DynamicGUIBench for applications whose interfaces change between actions, together with DynamicUI, an agent that processes screen recordings. The agent selects informative frames, filters inconsistent action reasoning and uses trajectory reflection for subsequent decisions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: WindowsWorld: A Process-Centric Benchmark of Autonomous GUI Agents in Professional Cross-Application Environments
summary: Introduces WindowsWorld for professional workflows spanning multiple desktop applications, with generated tasks refined through human review. Intermediate subgoals support process-oriented evaluation of cross-application reasoning and execution efficiency.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Desktop use is explicit; no additional operating-system claim is inferred solely from the benchmark name.

name: Faithful Mobile GUI Agents with Guided Advantage Estimator
summary: Introduces Faithful-Agent, which first teaches abstention under perturbed evidence and then refines GUI policies with an anchor-based, variance-adaptive advantage estimator. A thought-action consistency reward encourages decisions grounded in displayed evidence and instructions.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: AutoFocus: Uncertainty-Aware Active Visual Search for GUI Grounding
summary: Presents AutoFocus, a training-free grounding method that turns sampled coordinates and token uncertainty into spatial region proposals. Shape-aware crops and visual comparison select a target while retaining surrounding interface context.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Weblica: Scalable and Reproducible Training Environments for Visual Web Agents
summary: Introduces Weblica, which combines HTTP-level capture and replay with website-grounded environment synthesis. The resulting interactive web environments support reinforcement learning and tests of navigation transfer and inference-time scaling.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Region4Web: Rethinking Observation Space Granularity for Web Agents
summary: Reorganizes webpage accessibility trees into functional regions through hierarchical decomposition and semantic abstraction. PageDigest supplies a persistent region-level observation to web agents, evaluated on WebArena.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: Mem-W: Latent Memory-Native GUI Agents
summary: Introduces Mem-W, which compresses previous trajectories and current-session segments into latent memory tokens used directly by the GUI policy. Self-distillation and outcome supervision train this memory representation for web and mobile navigation.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: How Mobile World Model Guides GUI Agents?
summary: Compares mobile world models that predict state changes as delta text, full text, images or renderable code. Downstream Android benchmarks examine synthetic training trajectories and test-time guidance, including limits of post-action reflection.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ReVision: Scaling Computer-Use Agents via Temporal Visual Redundancy Reduction
summary: Trains GUI agents with a learned selector that removes repeated visual patches across consecutive screenshots while preserving spatial structure. ReVision evaluates this history representation on OSWorld, WebTailBench and AgentNetBench.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: OpenComputer: Verifiable Software Worlds for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Introduces OpenComputer, which builds desktop tasks around application-state verifiers and refines those verifiers using execution feedback. An evaluation harness records trajectories and assigns auditable partial credit across professional software workflows.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ScaleWoB: Guiding GUI Agents with Coding Agents via Large-Scale Environmental Synthesis
summary: Introduces ScaleWoB, which synthesizes interactive GUI environments as backend-free webpages with verifiable rewards. Its mobile-oriented benchmark evaluates agent execution and compares selected synthetic tasks with real-app behavior.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. Mobile, desktop and automotive interfaces are simulated as webpages; this does not assert native deployment on those platforms.

name: CUA-Gym: Scaling Verifiable Training Environments and Tasks for Computer-Use Agents
summary: Presents CUA-Gym, which co-generates instructions, initial and target states, and executable reward checks through generator-discriminator iterations. Mock web applications expand training environments, with learned agents evaluated on OSWorld-Verified and WebArena.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The abstract promises future open sourcing; this annotation does not independently verify artifact release or licensing.

name: MobileGym: A Verifiable and Highly Parallel Simulation Platform for Mobile GUI Agent Research
summary: Introduces MobileGym, a browser-hosted simulation of mobile app interactions whose configurable JSON state supports deterministic judging and parallel rollouts. MobileGym-Bench adds parameterized tasks, with experiments examining online training and transfer to real devices.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract. The simulator is browser-hosted; the abstract does not identify a native mobile operating system.

name: PhoneWorld: From Real-App Trajectories to Dynamic and Verifiable Environments for Phone-Use Agents
summary: Introduces PhoneWorld, which converts observed app pages, transitions and state changes into executable Android environments through a build-inspect-repair process. Generated tasks and programmatic verifiers support benchmarking, trajectory collection and online training.
notes: The annotation and scope were reviewed against the complete retained original arXiv abstract.

name: ASIL: Replacing Screenshot-and-Click with Structured State and Semantic Actions
summary: ASIL exposes application state as structured JSON and provides code-executable semantic actions. Its application benchmark compares this interface with screenshot control and application-native APIs, and studies supervised and reinforcement learning on the structured interface.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Syll: Open-Source Personal Automation with Cross-Surface Execution
summary: Syll combines tool calls, shell execution and visual GUI control in a personal-automation runtime. It turns user demonstrations into reusable skills and exposes execution logs, keyframes and approval checkpoints for inspection.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Exploring LLM Agent Designs and Interaction Modalities for Scientific Visualization
summary: This study compares specialized, computer-use and coding agents on scientific visualization workflows. It examines GUI, CLI, code and tool-call interaction modes, including how persistent memory changes performance across repeated trials.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: A Subgoal-driven Framework for Improving Long-Horizon LLM Agents
summary: The framework separates inference-time subgoal planning from MiRA, a reinforcement-learning method that supplies milestone rewards. WebArena-Lite experiments evaluate these mechanisms for long-horizon web navigation.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: TUA-Bench: A Benchmark for General-Purpose Terminal-Use Agents
summary: TUA-Bench evaluates terminal-use agents on general digital tasks, including document editing, email, web information seeking and specialist software workflows. Tasks run in real terminals with deterministic setup and execution-based scoring.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent general computer-operation benchmark: the evaluated interface is a terminal; GUI benchmarks are a contrast, not its execution modality.

name: Agent Skills for Large Language Models: Architecture, Acquisition, Security, and the Path Forward
summary: This survey organizes agent skills by architecture, acquisition, deployment and security, including their role in computer-use systems and GUI grounding. It also proposes a permission and lifecycle governance framework for skill deployment.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent survey of the skill layer: CUA deployment and GUI grounding are explicit parts of the review, but its overall scope extends well beyond interface agents.

name: GUI-GenBench: Evaluating Image Generation Models as Interactive GUI Environments
summary: GUI-GenBench tests image-generation models as action-conditioned GUI environments across five suites, including transitions, trajectories and grounding. Its VLM-based GUI-Score separates goal completion, interaction logic, consistency and visual properties.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: FocusUI: Efficient UI Grounding via Position-Preserving Visual Token Selection
summary: FocusUI selects instruction-relevant screenshot patches while preserving their positional structure for GUI grounding. Its PosPad scheme replaces runs of dropped tokens with positional markers and is evaluated under reduced token budgets.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Benchmarking LLM Judges for Mobile Agent Evaluation
summary: MobileJudgeBench compares completion judges against human labels on mobile-agent trajectories. It studies screenshot-sampling baselines, model-dependent error profiles and how judge quality relates to agent rankings and reinforcement-learning rewards.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: The Compliance Trap: Diagnosing How AI Agents Consume Conflicting Memory
summary: The Entry–Propagation–Recovery framework traces where conflicting memory first changes an agent action, how the effect propagates and whether recovery occurs. WebArena and the controlled MemTrapBench separate memory-consumption failures across these stages.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Agent Data Injection Attacks are Realistic Threats to AI Agents
summary: This study examines agent data injection, where untrusted content impersonates trusted metadata or tool-context data. It reports arbitrary-click vulnerabilities in web agents alongside separate coding-agent attacks, highlighting trust-boundary failures beyond instruction injection.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: DeskCraft: Benchmarking Desktop Agents on Professional Workflows and Human-in-the-Loop Collaboration
summary: DeskCraft evaluates professional desktop workflows and human-agent collaboration through mid-execution clarification, interruption and post-completion feedback. Its tasks cover creative applications and expose difficulties in long-horizon execution and proactive clarification.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: LongMemEval-V2: Evaluating Long-Term Agent Memory Toward Experienced Colleagues
summary: LongMemEval-V2 asks memory systems to recover environment knowledge from long web-agent histories for question answering. Its AgentRunbook variants contrast indexed knowledge pools with coding-agent retrieval from stored trajectory files.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: PlayCoder: Making LLM-Generated GUI Code Playable
summary: PlayEval measures whether generated GUI applications remain logically playable, using PlayTester to execute task-oriented GUI playthroughs. PlayCoder closes the loop between repository-aware generation, interactive testing and targeted code repair.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AJ-Bench: Benchmarking Agent-as-a-Judge for Environment-Aware Evaluation
summary: AJ-Bench evaluates judge agents that actively gather evidence from search, data systems and graphical interfaces. Its annotated tasks and trajectories test information acquisition, state verification and process verification.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: AgentClick: A Skill-Based Human-in-the-Loop Review Layer for Terminal AI Agents
summary: AgentClick gives terminal-based agents a browser review interface for plans, drafts, execution traces and editable memory. A local server and skill plugin let users inspect proposed actions and provide structured feedback.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent supervision interface: the browser UI is for human review of terminal agents; the abstract does not claim that those agents operate graphical interfaces.

name: MolmoPoint: Better Pointing for VLMs with Grounding Tokens
summary: MolmoPoint replaces textual coordinate generation with pointing tokens that select visual regions and refine them through subpatches. The general image/video method includes GUI-pointing evaluation on ScreenSpotPro alongside other visual grounding tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent general VLM pointing method with an explicit GUI-grounding experiment; no autonomous GUI-task execution is established.

name: CarePilot: A Multi-Agent Framework for Long-Horizon Computer Task Automation in Healthcare
summary: CareFlow benchmarks long healthcare-software workflows, while CarePilot coordinates action proposals, execution checks and corrective feedback using short- and long-term memory. Its actor consumes visual interfaces and system state to select semantic actions.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Terminal Is All You Need: Design Properties for Human-AI Agent Collaboration
summary: This position paper derives interface design principles from terminal-based human-agent collaboration: representational compatibility, transparent actions and low participation barriers. It argues that graphical and other agent-facing modalities should provide these properties explicitly.
verify_terms: Terminal Is All You Need: Design
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent conceptual HCI work about agent-facing interfaces; the abstract does not report GUI task experiments or a new evaluated CUA.

name: CovAgent: Overcoming the 30% Curse of Mobile Application Coverage with Agentic AI and Dynamic Instrumentation
summary: CovAgent augments Android GUI fuzzers by analyzing decompiled app code and component transitions to identify unsatisfied activation conditions. A second agent generates instrumentation that enables otherwise difficult-to-reach activities, with coverage-based evaluation.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Claw-Anything: Benchmarking Always-On Personal Assistants with Broader Access to User's Digital World
summary: Claw-Anything benchmarks persistent personal assistance across activity histories, backend services and integrated GUI/CLI interaction. Its simulated event histories introduce irrelevant or conflicting context, and a separate generation pipeline supplies training environments.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: VISTA: An End-to-End Benchmark for Visual Spec-to-Web-App Coding Agents
summary: VISTA evaluates coding agents that turn design handoffs into working web and Android applications. Its evaluator locates annotated interactive components and probes their behavior, keeping visual localization distinct from functional correctness.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent GUI-application generation benchmark with real component interaction probes; its main evaluated agents are application coders, not general GUI task executors.

name: MUIAnno: An Expert-Annotated Dataset and Evaluation Benchmark for Mobile UI Understanding
summary: MUIAnno provides expert labels for elements in manually explored mobile-app screens, with a web annotation tool that emits structured JSON. It also supplies UI-element detection baselines for the dataset.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: MMTB: Evaluating Terminal Agents on Multimedia-File Tasks
summary: MultiMedia-TerminalBench evaluates agents that use terminal tools to work with audio and video files. The Terminus-MM harness adds multimedia perception to study how accessible evidence changes executable workflows and task outcomes.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent computer-automation benchmark using terminal workflows, explicitly separated from graphical-interface control.

name: Beyond Screenshots: Evaluating VLMs' Understanding of UI Animations
summary: AniMINT evaluates how VLMs perceive, explain and interpret UI animations using densely annotated videos. The study distinguishes basic motion recognition from higher-level animation meaning and probes motion, context and perceptual cues.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: PixelPrune: Pixel-Level Adaptive Visual Token Reduction via Predictive Coding
summary: PixelPrune removes pixel-redundant patches before the vision encoder, reducing both encoding and downstream language-model work. The training-free method evaluates lossless and controlled-lossy compression on document and GUI tasks.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract. Adjacent cross-domain VLM compression method with actual GUI-benchmark evaluation; the abstract does not establish a full computer-use policy.

name: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition
summary: This public red-teaming study evaluates indirect prompt injection that both changes agent behavior and hides the compromise from the final response. Its scenarios include computer use alongside tool calling and coding, with analyses of transfer and model-dependent vulnerability.

name: MemoryArena: Benchmarking Agent Memory in Interdependent Multi-Session Agentic Tasks
summary: MemoryArena links tasks across sessions so that agents must distill earlier interaction experience and use it in later decisions. Its evaluation includes web navigation alongside planning, search and formal reasoning, testing memory through subsequent actions rather than recall alone.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: Nested Browser-Use Learning for Agentic Information Seeking
summary: NestBrowse organizes browser actions in a nested framework that separates interaction control from page exploration. It evaluates this design for deep information seeking beyond snippet retrieval and direct URL fetching.
notes: Reviewed against the complete retained official abstract.

name: ceLLMate: Sandboxing Browser AI Agents
summary: ceLLMate constrains browser-agent authority through an extension that applies policies at the HTTP layer. It evaluates this sandbox against prompt-injection attacks in WASP, avoiding dependence on brittle low-level click and keystroke policies.
